980	// Visible answers what a reader would see at one slot, stamp included.
981	//
982	// Fields answers the decode's question, names and bytes for one record. This
983	// answers a conformance harness's: one slot at a time, plus the stamp that
984	// decided it, which a suite comparing two projections has to see.
985	func (p *RecordProjection) Visible(k record.Key, field string) (record.Value, bool, error) {
986		var v record.Value
987		var lamport, seq int64
988		var deleted bool
989		err := p.reader().QueryRow(p.readCtx(),
990			`SELECT f.value, f.version, f.deleted, f.lamport, f.writer, f.seq
991			 FROM repo_record_fields f
992			 LEFT JOIN repo_record_floors fl
993			        ON fl.repo_id = f.repo_id AND fl.schema_name = f.schema_name
994			       AND fl.type = f.type AND fl.id = f.id
995			 WHERE f.repo_id = $1 AND f.schema_name = $2 AND f.type = $3 AND f.id = $4 AND f.field = $5
996			   AND (fl.repo_id IS NULL OR (f.lamport, f.writer, f.seq) > (fl.lamport, fl.writer, fl.seq))`,
997			p.repoID, p.schemaName, k.Type, k.ID, field).
998			Scan(&v.Bytes, &v.Version, &deleted, &lamport, &v.Stamp.Writer, &seq)
999		switch {
1000		case errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows):
1001			return record.Value{}, false, nil
1002		case err != nil:
1003			// Before the deleted check, so a Scan that failed half-way cannot be
1004			// read as an answer.
1005			return record.Value{}, false, err
1006		case deleted:
1007			return record.Value{}, false, nil
1008		}
1009		v.Stamp.L, v.Stamp.Seq = uint64(lamport), uint64(seq)
1010		return v, true, nil
1011	}

1013	// Apply takes a batch a caller already holds, which Tick is otherwise the only
1014	// route to. A conformance harness has its own; so would a backfill replaying a
1015	// captured feed.
1016	func (p *RecordProjection) Apply(ctx context.Context, b project.Batch) error {
1017		_, err := p.Tick(ctx, heldBatch{b})
1018		return err
1019	}

18	// The records routes: a read-only view of a repo's entire-records stores —
19	// schema-described records held in strata stores (refs/strata/<schema>/),
20	// served from this cell's projection of them. They are served on the v0 surface
21	// (APIv0Base), not v1: the shapes are not settled yet.
22	//
23	// A thin adapter over internal/records, which owns the read and its paging, over
24	// internal/recordprojection, which keeps the projection current. Reads gate on repo pull and are authenticated-only: a records
25	// store carries arbitrary user data with no per-record access control, so the
26	// whole store is exactly as readable as the repo, and this stays off the
27	// anonymous public surface for the same reason git-meta does.
28	//
29	// The response bodies embed entire-records' own DTOs rather than mirroring them,
30	// so entire-api's wire shape cannot drift from the decode that produces it. The
31	// OpenAPI component names are therefore that package's (RecordDTO, SchemaDTO),
32	// renamed for the gateway by schemanames.go.
33	
34	// RecordsReader is the records surface the routes need, satisfied by
35	// *records.Reader. A fake stands in for route tests.
36	type RecordsReader interface {
37		ListSchemas(ctx context.Context, repoID string, page records.Page) (records.SchemasResult, error)
38		Schema(ctx context.Context, repoID, address string) (records.SchemaResult, error)
39		Collections(ctx context.Context, repoID, address string, types []string, page records.Page) (records.CollectionsResult, error)
40		Collection(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, typeName string, page records.Page) (records.CollectionResult, error)
41		Record(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, typeName, id string) (records.RecordResult, error)
42		Changes(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, token string, opts records.ChangesOptions) (records.ChangesResult, error)
43	}

45	// RecordsSchemaSummary is one schema a repo holds.

48	type RecordsSchemaSummary struct {
49		Name string `json:"name" doc:"Schema name, as used in the {schema} path segment"`
50		Tip  string `json:"tip" doc:"Names the store's current state"`
51	}

53	// RepoRecordsListSchemasInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/records.
54	type RepoRecordsListSchemasInput struct {
55		RepoID string `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
56		RecordsPage
57	}

59	// RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput lists the repo's records schemas. No ETag: the
60	// listing spans every store, so there is no one state for it to name.

62		Body struct {
63			Items         []RecordsSchemaSummary `json:"items"`
64			NextPageToken string                 `json:"nextPageToken,omitempty"`
65		}
66	}

68	// RecordsPage is the pagination pair every list read here shares.
69	//
70	// Exported, and it has to be: huma resolves parameters by walking the input
71	// struct's exported fields, and an embedded field takes its type's name — so an
72	// unexported type embeds as an unexported field, which the walk skips silently.
73	//
74	// The token carries the state its scan started at along with the scope it
75	// covers. A continuation after the store has moved is refused with 409, and the
76	// caller restarts; a token that contradicts an explicit types list is refused
77	// rather than silently answering a different question.
78	type RecordsPage struct {
79		PageSize  int    `query:"pageSize" minimum:"1" maximum:"100" default:"50" doc:"Maximum records per page"`
80		PageToken string `query:"pageToken" doc:"Cursor from a previous page's nextPageToken"`
81	}

91		ETag string `header:"ETag"`
92		Body struct {
93			Tip     string `json:"tip" doc:"Names the state of the store this response was read from"`
94			Version int    `json:"version" doc:"Version of the schema, counting the breaking changes it has survived"`
95			// Named TypeModel rather than Schema: huma builds the response's
96			// $schema link by prepending a struct field of its own called Schema,
97			// and a body field with that Go name collides — reflect.StructOf
98			// panics, huma recovers, and the link is silently dropped. The wire key
99			// is unaffected.
100			TypeModel recordapi.SchemaDTO `json:"schema"`
101		}
102	}

117	// well-defined boundary. Paging bounds the response; a page still reads every
118	// record of the types it spans.

121		Body struct {
122			Tip           string                `json:"tip" doc:"Names the state of the store this page was read from; every page of one scan carries the same tip"`

153	// own: the access gate resolves it by name (authz.go's requireRepoAccess reads
154	// hctx.Param("repo_id")), so renaming it on these routes alone would hand the
155	// gate an empty id. It is one spelling across 95 route declarations; changing

173	// registerRepoRecords wires the records read routes onto api, the v0 surface.
174	// repoOp bundles the access gate (repoReadGate: authn + repo pull, the same gate
175	// as registerRepos' reads), so none of these can be registered ungated.
176	func registerRepoRecords(api huma.API, deps *RepoActivityDeps) {
177		gate := repoReadGate(api, deps)
178		repoOp := func(id, method, path, summary, tag string) huma.Operation {
179			return teamOp(api, id, method, path, summary, tag, gate)
180		}
181		// 404: the repo is not in this region (the gate), or no schema by that name.
182		// 409: a page token the store has moved past; restart from the first page.
183		// 429: the per-IP read-through throttle. 502: catching the projection up
184		// over git failed.
185		extra := []int{http.StatusNotFound, http.StatusConflict, http.StatusTooManyRequests, http.StatusBadGateway}
186	
187		listOp := repoOp("repoRecordsListSchemas", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records",
188			"List the repository's records schemas", "records")
189		listOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(listOp.Errors, extra...)
190		huma.Register(api, listOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsListSchemasInput) (*RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput, error) {
191			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
192			if err != nil {
193				return nil, err
194			}
195			found, err := reader.ListSchemas(ctx, in.RepoID, records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
196			if err != nil {
197				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
198			}
199			out := &RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput{}
200			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
201			out.Body.Items = make([]RecordsSchemaSummary, 0, len(found.Schemas))
202			for _, s := range found.Schemas {
203				out.Body.Items = append(out.Body.Items, RecordsSchemaSummary{Name: s.Name, Tip: s.Tip})
204			}
205			return out, nil
206		})
207	
208		schemaOp := repoOp("repoRecordsSchema", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}",
209			"Read a records schema's type model", "records")
210		schemaOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(schemaOp.Errors, extra...)
211		huma.Register(api, schemaOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsSchemaInput) (*RepoRecordsSchemaOutput, error) {
212			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
213			if err != nil {
214				return nil, err
215			}
216			res, err := reader.Schema(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema)
217			if err != nil {
218				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
219			}
220			out := &RepoRecordsSchemaOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
221			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
222			out.Body.Version = res.Version
223			out.Body.TypeModel = res.Schema
224			return out, nil
225		})
226	
227		collectionsOp := repoOp("repoRecordsCollections", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections",
228			"Read several types' records from one state of the store", "records")
229		collectionsOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(collectionsOp.Errors, extra...)
230		huma.Register(api, collectionsOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsCollectionsInput) (*RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput, error) {
231			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
232			if err != nil {
233				return nil, err
234			}
235			// splitCSV (changes.go), because huma's `explode` reads repeated
236			// parameters only and never splits on commas — without it the
237			// documented `?types=a,b` spelling arrives as one type named "a,b"
238			// and is refused by name, an error about a type nobody asked for.
239			res, err := reader.Collections(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, splitCSV(in.Types),
240				records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
241			if err != nil {
242				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
243			}
244			out := &RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
245			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
246			out.Body.ChangesToken = res.ChangesToken
247			out.Body.Items = res.Records
248			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
249			return out, nil
250		})
251	
252		collectionOp := repoOp("repoRecordsCollection", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}",
253			"Read one type's records", "records")
254		collectionOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(collectionOp.Errors, extra...)
255		huma.Register(api, collectionOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsCollectionInput) (*RepoRecordsCollectionOutput, error) {
256			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
257			if err != nil {
258				return nil, err
259			}
260			res, err := reader.Collection(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, in.Type,
261				records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
262			if err != nil {
263				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
264			}
265			out := &RepoRecordsCollectionOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
266			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
267			out.Body.Type = res.Type
268			out.Body.Items = res.Records
269			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
270			return out, nil
271		})
272	
273		getOp := repoOp("repoRecordsGet", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}/{recordId}",
274			"Read one record with its children and nested records", "records")
275		getOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(getOp.Errors, extra...)
276		huma.Register(api, getOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsGetInput) (*RepoRecordsGetOutput, error) {
277			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
278			if err != nil {
279				return nil, err
280			}
281			res, err := reader.Record(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, in.Type, in.RecordID)
282			if err != nil {
283				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
284			}
285			out := &RepoRecordsGetOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
286			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
287			out.Body.Record = res.Record
288			return out, nil
289		})
290	}
291	
292	// EnableRecords wires the records routes: reads from this cell's projection of
293	// the repo's strata stores, caught up by fetching the store over git as the
294	// caller, through the same per-request content transport the other
295	// read-throughs use. Call after ContentBaseTransport / ContentTransport are set.
296	func (deps *RepoActivityDeps) EnableRecords() error {
297		if deps.RepoAPIBase == "" || deps.Store == nil {
298			return nil
299		}
300		origin, err := deps.gitOrigin()
301		if err != nil {
302			return fmt.Errorf("records: %w", err)
303		}
304		deps.RecordsReader = records.New(recordprojection.Reads{
305			Store: deps.Store,
306			Remote: func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) stratagit.Remote {
307				return stratagit.Remote{URL: origin + "/git/repo/" + url.PathEscape(repoID), Client: contentHTTPClient(ctx, deps)}
308			},
309		})
310		return nil
311	}
312	
313	// recordsReader is the prologue every records handler shares.
314	func recordsReader(deps *RepoActivityDeps) (RecordsReader, error) {
315		if deps.RecordsReader == nil {
316			return nil, huma.Error500InternalServerError("records not configured", errors.New("RecordsReader nil"))
317		}
318		return deps.RecordsReader, nil
319	}
320	
321	// recordsHTTPError maps a records read's failures onto statuses: the store's own
322	// absence, a page token the store has moved past, then entire-records'
323	// invalid/not-found verdicts via recordapi.StatusFor — the function its own
324	// surface uses — and anything else as the read upstream failing.
325	func recordsHTTPError(err error) error {
326		switch {
327		case errors.Is(err, records.ErrNoSchema):
328			return huma.Error404NotFound(err.Error())
329		case errors.Is(err, records.ErrStoreMoved):
330			return huma.Error409Conflict(err.Error())
331		}
332		return recordsVerdict(err, "records read failed")
333	}
334	
335	// recordsVerdict maps entire-records' verdicts onto 400/404 and the rest,
336	// failed round trips to entiredb, onto a 502.
337	func recordsVerdict(err error, upstream string) error {
338		switch recordapi.StatusFor(err) {
339		case http.StatusBadRequest:
340			return huma.Error400BadRequest(err.Error())
341		case http.StatusNotFound:
342			return huma.Error404NotFound(err.Error())
343		}
344		return huma.Error502BadGateway(upstream, err)
345	}

16	// changes stream or write socket: from entiredb stamping the ref event to the
17	// read it rang being answered. It spans entiredb's outbox relay, NATS, the hub
18	// and the catch-up read, which no single span covers. otelsetup buckets it by

28		oldest := oldestEvent(rang)
29		if oldest.IsZero() {
30			return
31		}

40		var oldest time.Time

42			if !ev.Timestamp.IsZero() && (oldest.IsZero() || ev.Timestamp.Before(oldest)) {
43				oldest = ev.Timestamp
44			}
45		}
46		return oldest
47	}

50		switch {
51		case res.Reload:

53		case res.Empty():

55		}

18	// The records routes: a read-only view of a repo's entire-records stores —
19	// schema-described records held in strata stores (refs/strata/<schema>/),
20	// served from this cell's projection of them. They are served on the v0 surface
21	// (APIv0Base), not v1: the shapes are not settled yet.
22	//
23	// A thin adapter over internal/records, which owns the read and its paging, over
24	// internal/recordprojection, which keeps the projection current. Reads gate on repo pull and are authenticated-only: a records
25	// store carries arbitrary user data with no per-record access control, so the
26	// whole store is exactly as readable as the repo, and this stays off the
27	// anonymous public surface for the same reason git-meta does.
28	//
29	// The response bodies embed entire-records' own DTOs rather than mirroring them,
30	// so entire-api's wire shape cannot drift from the decode that produces it. The
31	// OpenAPI component names are therefore that package's (RecordDTO, SchemaDTO),
32	// renamed for the gateway by schemanames.go.
33	
34	// RecordsReader is the records surface the routes need, satisfied by
35	// *records.Reader. A fake stands in for route tests.
36	type RecordsReader interface {
37		ListSchemas(ctx context.Context, repoID string, page records.Page) (records.SchemasResult, error)
38		Schema(ctx context.Context, repoID, address string) (records.SchemaResult, error)
39		Collections(ctx context.Context, repoID, address string, types []string, page records.Page) (records.CollectionsResult, error)
40		Collection(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, typeName string, page records.Page) (records.CollectionResult, error)
41		Record(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, typeName, id string) (records.RecordResult, error)
42		Changes(ctx context.Context, repoID, address, token string, opts records.ChangesOptions) (records.ChangesResult, error)
43	}

45	// RecordsSchemaSummary is one schema a repo holds.
46	//
47	// No version here; the schema read reports it.
48	type RecordsSchemaSummary struct {
49		Name string `json:"name" doc:"Schema name, as used in the {schema} path segment"`
50		Tip  string `json:"tip" doc:"Names the store's current state"`
51	}
52	
53	// RepoRecordsListSchemasInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/records.
54	type RepoRecordsListSchemasInput struct {
55		RepoID string `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
56		RecordsPage
57	}

59	// RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput lists the repo's records schemas. No ETag: the
60	// listing spans every store, so there is no one state for it to name.

64			NextPageToken string                 `json:"nextPageToken,omitempty"`
65		}
66	}

68	// RecordsPage is the pagination pair every list read here shares.
69	//
70	// Exported, and it has to be: huma resolves parameters by walking the input
71	// struct's exported fields, and an embedded field takes its type's name — so an
72	// unexported type embeds as an unexported field, which the walk skips silently.
73	//
74	// The token carries the state its scan started at along with the scope it
75	// covers. A continuation after the store has moved is refused with 409, and the
76	// caller restarts; a token that contradicts an explicit types list is refused
77	// rather than silently answering a different question.
78	type RecordsPage struct {
79		PageSize  int    `query:"pageSize" minimum:"1" maximum:"100" default:"50" doc:"Maximum records per page"`
80		PageToken string `query:"pageToken" doc:"Cursor from a previous page's nextPageToken"`
81	}

85		RepoID string `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
86		Schema string `path:"schema" doc:"Schema name"`
87	}

89	// RepoRecordsSchemaOutput is a schema's type model and the state it was read from.

91		ETag string `header:"ETag"`
92		Body struct {
93			Tip     string `json:"tip" doc:"Names the state of the store this response was read from"`
94			Version int    `json:"version" doc:"Version of the schema, counting the breaking changes it has survived"`
95			// Named TypeModel rather than Schema: huma builds the response's
96			// $schema link by prepending a struct field of its own called Schema,
97			// and a body field with that Go name collides — reflect.StructOf
98			// panics, huma recovers, and the link is silently dropped. The wire key
99			// is unaffected.
100			TypeModel recordapi.SchemaDTO `json:"schema"`
101		}
102	}
103	
104	// RepoRecordsCollectionsInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections.
105	type RepoRecordsCollectionsInput struct {
106		RepoID string   `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
107		Schema string   `path:"schema" doc:"Schema name"`
108		Types  []string `query:"types,explode" doc:"Type names to read (repeatable or comma-separated). Omit for every type the schema declares, nested types included."`
109		RecordsPage
110	}

112	// RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput is one page of records, all from one state of the
113	// store.
114	//
115	// A flat list rather than a map keyed by type: every record names its own type,
116	// so grouping stays the client's to do, and a page of a map of arrays has no
117	// well-defined boundary. Paging bounds the response; a page still reads every
118	// record of the types it spans.
119	type RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput struct {
120		ETag string `header:"ETag"`
121		Body struct {
122			Tip           string                `json:"tip" doc:"Names the state of the store this page was read from; every page of one scan carries the same tip"`
123			ChangesToken  string                `json:"changesToken" doc:"Where GET …/changes continues from this state, as its changes_token"`
124			Items         []recordapi.RecordDTO `json:"items"`
125			NextPageToken string                `json:"nextPageToken,omitempty"`
126		}
127	}
128	
129	// RepoRecordsCollectionInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}.
130	type RepoRecordsCollectionInput struct {
131		RepoID string `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
132		Schema string `path:"schema" doc:"Schema name"`
133		Type   string `path:"type" doc:"Type name, as declared by the schema"`
134		RecordsPage
135	}
136	
137	// RepoRecordsCollectionOutput is one page of a single type's records.
138	type RepoRecordsCollectionOutput struct {
139		ETag string `header:"ETag"`
140		Body struct {
141			Tip           string                `json:"tip"`
142			Type          string                `json:"type"`
143			Items         []recordapi.RecordDTO `json:"items"`
144			NextPageToken string                `json:"nextPageToken,omitempty"`
145		}
146	}

148	// RepoRecordsGetInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}/{recordId}.
149	//
150	// recordId is camelCase, which is the rule (CASING-002) and the dominant
151	// spelling for a resource id here — reviewId, commentId, trailId, threadId and
152	// the rest. repo_id is the exception, and not one this surface may fix on its
153	// own: the access gate resolves it by name (authz.go's requireRepoAccess reads
154	// hctx.Param("repo_id")), so renaming it on these routes alone would hand the
155	// gate an empty id. It is one spelling across 95 route declarations; changing
156	// it is a platform-wide change, not a records one.
157	type RepoRecordsGetInput struct {
158		RepoID   string `path:"repo_id" doc:"Repo id: placement ULID or public repo_<group ULID>"`
159		Schema   string `path:"schema" doc:"Schema name"`
160		Type     string `path:"type" doc:"Type name, as declared by the schema"`
161		RecordID string `path:"recordId" doc:"Record id (ULID). A nested record is read from its container's response, not here."`
162	}
163	
164	// RepoRecordsGetOutput is one record with its children and nested records.
165	type RepoRecordsGetOutput struct {
166		ETag string `header:"ETag"`
167		Body struct {
168			Tip    string                    `json:"tip"`
169			Record recordapi.RecordDetailDTO `json:"record"`
170		}
171	}
172	
173	// registerRepoRecords wires the records read routes onto api, the v0 surface.
174	// repoOp bundles the access gate (repoReadGate: authn + repo pull, the same gate
175	// as registerRepos' reads), so none of these can be registered ungated.
176	func registerRepoRecords(api huma.API, deps *RepoActivityDeps) {
177		gate := repoReadGate(api, deps)
178		repoOp := func(id, method, path, summary, tag string) huma.Operation {
179			return teamOp(api, id, method, path, summary, tag, gate)
180		}
181		// 404: the repo is not in this region (the gate), or no schema by that name.
182		// 409: a page token the store has moved past; restart from the first page.
183		// 429: the per-IP read-through throttle. 502: catching the projection up
184		// over git failed.
185		extra := []int{http.StatusNotFound, http.StatusConflict, http.StatusTooManyRequests, http.StatusBadGateway}
186	
187		listOp := repoOp("repoRecordsListSchemas", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records",
188			"List the repository's records schemas", "records")
189		listOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(listOp.Errors, extra...)
190		huma.Register(api, listOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsListSchemasInput) (*RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput, error) {
191			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
192			if err != nil {
193				return nil, err
194			}
195			found, err := reader.ListSchemas(ctx, in.RepoID, records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
196			if err != nil {
197				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
198			}
199			out := &RepoRecordsListSchemasOutput{}
200			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
201			out.Body.Items = make([]RecordsSchemaSummary, 0, len(found.Schemas))
202			for _, s := range found.Schemas {
203				out.Body.Items = append(out.Body.Items, RecordsSchemaSummary{Name: s.Name, Tip: s.Tip})
204			}
205			return out, nil
206		})
207	
208		schemaOp := repoOp("repoRecordsSchema", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}",
209			"Read a records schema's type model", "records")
210		schemaOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(schemaOp.Errors, extra...)
211		huma.Register(api, schemaOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsSchemaInput) (*RepoRecordsSchemaOutput, error) {
212			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
213			if err != nil {
214				return nil, err
215			}
216			res, err := reader.Schema(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema)
217			if err != nil {
218				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
219			}
220			out := &RepoRecordsSchemaOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
221			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
222			out.Body.Version = res.Version
223			out.Body.TypeModel = res.Schema
224			return out, nil
225		})
226	
227		collectionsOp := repoOp("repoRecordsCollections", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections",
228			"Read several types' records from one state of the store", "records")
229		collectionsOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(collectionsOp.Errors, extra...)
230		huma.Register(api, collectionsOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsCollectionsInput) (*RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput, error) {
231			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
232			if err != nil {
233				return nil, err
234			}
235			// splitCSV (changes.go), because huma's `explode` reads repeated
236			// parameters only and never splits on commas — without it the
237			// documented `?types=a,b` spelling arrives as one type named "a,b"
238			// and is refused by name, an error about a type nobody asked for.
239			res, err := reader.Collections(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, splitCSV(in.Types),
240				records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
241			if err != nil {
242				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
243			}
244			out := &RepoRecordsCollectionsOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
245			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
246			out.Body.ChangesToken = res.ChangesToken
247			out.Body.Items = res.Records
248			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
249			return out, nil
250		})
251	
252		collectionOp := repoOp("repoRecordsCollection", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}",
253			"Read one type's records", "records")
254		collectionOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(collectionOp.Errors, extra...)
255		huma.Register(api, collectionOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsCollectionInput) (*RepoRecordsCollectionOutput, error) {
256			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
257			if err != nil {
258				return nil, err
259			}
260			res, err := reader.Collection(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, in.Type,
261				records.Page{Size: in.PageSize, Token: in.PageToken})
262			if err != nil {
263				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
264			}
265			out := &RepoRecordsCollectionOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
266			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
267			out.Body.Type = res.Type
268			out.Body.Items = res.Records
269			out.Body.NextPageToken = REDACTED
270			return out, nil
271		})
272	
273		getOp := repoOp("repoRecordsGet", http.MethodGet, "/repos/{repo_id}/records/{schema}/collections/{type}/{recordId}",
274			"Read one record with its children and nested records", "records")
275		getOp.Errors = withExtraErrors(getOp.Errors, extra...)
276		huma.Register(api, getOp, func(ctx context.Context, in *RepoRecordsGetInput) (*RepoRecordsGetOutput, error) {
277			reader, err := recordsReader(deps)
278			if err != nil {
279				return nil, err
280			}
281			res, err := reader.Record(ctx, in.RepoID, in.Schema, in.Type, in.RecordID)
282			if err != nil {
283				return nil, recordsHTTPError(err)
284			}
285			out := &RepoRecordsGetOutput{ETag: etag(res.Tip)}
286			out.Body.Tip = res.Tip
287			out.Body.Record = res.Record
288			return out, nil
289		})
290	}
291	
292	// EnableRecords wires the records routes: reads from this cell's projection of
293	// the repo's strata stores, caught up by fetching the store over git as the
294	// caller, through the same per-request content transport the other
295	// read-throughs use. Call after ContentBaseTransport / ContentTransport are set.
296	func (deps *RepoActivityDeps) EnableRecords() error {
297		if deps.RepoAPIBase == "" || deps.Store == nil {
298			return nil
299		}
300		origin, err := deps.gitOrigin()
301		if err != nil {
302			return fmt.Errorf("records: %w", err)
303		}
304		deps.RecordsReader = records.New(recordprojection.Reads{
305			Store: deps.Store,
306			Remote: func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) stratagit.Remote {
307				return stratagit.Remote{URL: origin + "/git/repo/" + url.PathEscape(repoID), Client: contentHTTPClient(ctx, deps)}
308			},
309		})
310		return nil
311	}
312	
313	// recordsReader is the prologue every records handler shares.
314	func recordsReader(deps *RepoActivityDeps) (RecordsReader, error) {
315		if deps.RecordsReader == nil {
316			return nil, huma.Error500InternalServerError("records not configured", errors.New("RecordsReader nil"))
317		}
318		return deps.RecordsReader, nil
319	}
320	
321	// recordsHTTPError maps a records read's failures onto statuses: the store's own
322	// absence, a page token the store has moved past, then entire-records'
323	// invalid/not-found verdicts via recordapi.StatusFor — the function its own
324	// surface uses — and anything else as the read upstream failing.
325	func recordsHTTPError(err error) error {
326		switch {
327		case errors.Is(err, records.ErrNoSchema):
328			return huma.Error404NotFound(err.Error())
329		case errors.Is(err, records.ErrStoreMoved):
330			return huma.Error409Conflict(err.Error())
331		}
332		return recordsVerdict(err, "records read failed")
333	}
334	
335	// recordsVerdict maps entire-records' verdicts onto 400/404 and the rest,
336	// failed round trips to entiredb, onto a 502.
337	func recordsVerdict(err error, upstream string) error {
338		switch recordapi.StatusFor(err) {
339		case http.StatusBadRequest:
340			return huma.Error400BadRequest(err.Error())
341		case http.StatusNotFound:
342			return huma.Error404NotFound(err.Error())
343		}
344		return huma.Error502BadGateway(upstream, err)
345	}

1	package httpapi
2	
3	// SSE (text/event-stream) live ref-change stream: GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs/events.
4	//
5	// Unlike the DB-polling SSE families (reviews_events_sse.go, threads_events_sse.go —
6	// one shared poll per resource, fanned out to every connection), this hub is
7	// push-driven: it owns one shared core NATS subscription per repo_id
8	// (internal/refstream, subject repo_refs_v1.{repo_id}), fed by entiredb's
9	// live ref-push stream, and fans debounced events out to every connection
10	// watching that repo — so N viewers of a hot repo cost one subscription, not
11	// N, the same "one shared drain" leverage as the poll-based hubs, just
12	// sourced from NATS instead of a store poll.
13	//
14	// Design, decided after exploring alternatives (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY was a
15	// lower-infra-cost option; not chosen because it was scoped for a
16	// low-latency signal at real scale):
17	//   - Source: a plain core (non-JetStream) NATS subscription, not a durable
18	//     JetStream consumer — at-most-once delivery is the right contract for a
19	//     live tail where a client re-syncs current state on every reconnect
20	//     rather than replaying history. See internal/refstream.
21	//   - Debounce: rapid updates to the SAME ref are coalesced to at most one
22	//     flush per refDebounceWindow (leaky-bucket: the first update schedules a
23	//     flush; further updates before it fires just replace the pending
24	//     payload, latest wins), computed ONCE in the hub and fanned out — so a
25	//     hot repo with many viewers doesn't multiply (raw update rate × viewer
26	//     count) into unbounded per-connection work. A doorbell (addDoorbell) is
27	//     rung at once instead: it renders no event, only reads what moved, and
28	//     its one-slot wake already folds a burst into the next read. The
29	//     debounce never merged across refs: each ref has its own timer, so a
30	//     burst over several refs flushed with the spacing it arrived with.
31	//   - No persisted history, no cursor, no catch-up walk (unlike the
32	//     poll-based hubs): this is a live-only signal. A connection's initial
33	//     state comes from a one-time live entiredb ListRefsWithSymrefs read (the
34	//     "snapshot" frame) — NOT repo_branch_tip, which only tracks branches
35	//     and never resolves symref targets — filtered by the same `prefix` the
36	//     connection requested, matching GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs's own
37	//     repeatable prefix convention (api/repov1.ListRefsInput, entiredb) so a
38	//     client that already knows that filter gets it for free here. symrefs=true
39	//     so a HEAD entry's symrefTarget is actually populated in the snapshot.
40	//   - Re-auth: unlike a poll-driven hub (which gets re-auth "for free" every
41	//     poll tick), a push-driven connection has no natural tick — a quiet
42	//     repo could go minutes between NATS messages — so each connection runs
43	//     its own ~ssePollInterval re-auth timer via the same shared
44	//     cachedStreamAuth cache the poll-based hubs use.
45	import (
46		"context"
47		"errors"
48		"net/http"
49		"strings"
50		"sync"
51		"time"
52	
53		"github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2"
54		"github.com/entirehq/entiredb/modules/apidocs"
55		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
56	
57		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/ingest"
58		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/refstream"
59		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/repoapi"
60	)
61	
62	// refDebounceWindow bounds how long a burst of rapid updates to the SAME ref
63	// can be coalesced into one delivered event: the first update to a quiet ref
64	// schedules a flush at most this far out; any further update to that ref
65	// before the flush fires just replaces the pending payload (latest wins)
66	// instead of rescheduling the timer, so a continuously hot ref still flushes
67	// on a steady ~refDebounceWindow cadence rather than waiting for a quiet
68	// moment that never comes. A package var (not a const), matching
69	// ssePollInterval et al. in reviews_events_sse.go, so a test can shrink it to
70	// run in milliseconds.
71	var refDebounceWindow = 200 * time.Millisecond
72	
73	// RefEventsInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs/events.
74	type RefEventsInput struct {
75		RepoID string `path:"repo_id"`
76		// Prefix mirrors GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs's own repeatable prefix filter
77		// verbatim (api/repov1.ListRefsInput, entiredb): query:"prefix,explode",
78		// maxItems 100, empty = every ref.
79		Prefix []string `query:"prefix,explode" maxItems:"100" doc:"Ref-name prefixes to filter by (repeatable), e.g. \"refs/heads/\", \"refs/tags/\", \"HEAD\" — the same convention as GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs. Empty streams every ref."`
80	}
81	
82	// refSnapshotEntryJSON/refSnapshotData/refDeltaData are the SSE payloads,
83	// camelCase per CASING-001 (matching toReviewEventJSON/toThreadEventJSON).
84	
85	type refSnapshotEntryJSON struct {
86		Name         string `json:"name"`
87		OID          string `json:"oid,omitempty"`
88		SymrefTarget string `json:"symrefTarget,omitempty"`
89	}
90	
91	type refSnapshotData struct {
92		Refs []refSnapshotEntryJSON `json:"refs"`
93	}
94	
95	// refDeltaData is one live ref-change event, projected from ingest.RefEvent.
96	// The SSE `event:` name is normally the ref op itself (create/update/
97	// force_update/delete/symref_update — entiredb's refevents.RefOp* wire
98	// values), mirroring the review/thread hubs' convention of using the event's
99	// own type as the frame name — but see refFrameEvent for why the frame name
100	// is validated first. RefOp is also carried in the JSON body regardless, so a
101	// client can always recover the real op even on the rare refFallbackOp path.
102	type refDeltaData struct {
103		RefName         string `json:"refName"`
104		RefOp           string `json:"refOp"`
105		OldTarget       string `json:"oldTarget,omitempty"`
106		NewTarget       string `json:"newTarget,omitempty"`
107		OldSymrefTarget string `json:"oldSymrefTarget,omitempty"`
108		NewSymrefTarget string `json:"newSymrefTarget,omitempty"`
109		PusherID        string `json:"pusherId,omitempty"`
110		EventAt         string `json:"eventAt"`
111	}
112	
113	func toRefDeltaData(ev ingest.RefEvent) refDeltaData {
114		return refDeltaData{
115			RefName:         ev.RefName,
116			RefOp:           ev.RefOp,
117			OldTarget:       ev.OldTarget,
118			NewTarget:       ev.NewTarget,
119			OldSymrefTarget: ev.OldSymrefTarget,
120			NewSymrefTarget: ev.NewSymrefTarget,
121			PusherID:        ev.PusherID,
122			EventAt:         isoMillis(ev.Timestamp),
123		}
124	}
125	
126	// refKnownOps is the closed set of ref_op wire values entiredb's envelope
127	// version 1 ever publishes on repo_refs_v1 (refevents.RefOp{Create,Update,
128	// Delete,ForceUpdate}, plus internal/ingest's own unexported
129	// refOpSymrefUpdate — both mirrored here as literals since neither package
130	// exports them for this use).
131	var refKnownOps = map[string]bool{
132		"create": true, "update": true, "delete": true, "force_update": true,
133		"symref_update": true,
134	}
135	
136	// refFallbackOp substitutes for any ref_op outside refKnownOps.
137	const refFallbackOp = "ref_change"
138	
139	// refFrameEvent returns refOp verbatim if it's one of refKnownOps, else
140	// refFallbackOp. ev.RefOp is decoded straight from an external NATS payload
141	// with no format check (ingest.ParseRefEvent), and sseWriter.frame
142	// (reviews_events_sse.go) builds a frame by raw string concatenation with no
143	// escaping — unlike the DB-polling hubs, whose event: name always comes from
144	// an internal, store-constrained enum. Without this check, a ref_op
145	// containing "\n"/"\r" would inject extra lines into the frame, corrupting it
146	// for every connection sharing that repo's hub. The real value is never lost
147	// even on the fallback path — refDeltaData.RefOp (JSON-escaped, so safe
148	// regardless of its content) always carries it too.
149	func refFrameEvent(refOp string) string {
150		if refKnownOps[refOp] {
151			return refOp
152		}
153		return refFallbackOp
154	}
155	
156	// ---- shared per-repo push drain ----
157	
158	// refEventHubs is shared so a repo costs one NATS subscription per replica.
159	func (deps *RepoActivityDeps) refEventHubs() *refHubRegistry {
160		deps.refHubsOnce.Do(func() {
161			deps.refHubs = newRefHubRegistry(func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error) {
162				return refstream.Subscribe(ctx, deps.RefEventsNATS, repoID)
163			})
164			deps.refHubs.reconnected = func() (<-chan nats.Status, func()) {
165				return refstream.Reconnected(deps.RefEventsNATS)
166			}
167		})
168		return deps.refHubs
169	}
170	
171	// refHubRegistry maps a repo_id to its live per-replica ref-events hub,
172	// ref-counted so a hub is created (and subscribed) on the first connection
173	// and torn down when the last leaves — the push-driven counterpart of
174	// changeHubRegistry (reviews_events_sse.go): one shared NATS subscription per
175	// repo, never one per connection.
176	type refHubRegistry struct {
177		mu          sync.Mutex
178		hubs        map[string]*refHub
179		subscribe   func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error)
180		reconnected func() (<-chan nats.Status, func())
181	}
182	
183	func newRefHubRegistry(subscribe func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error)) *refHubRegistry {
184		return &refHubRegistry{hubs: map[string]*refHub{}, subscribe: subscribe}
185	}
186	
187	// acquire returns the live hub for repoID, subscribing and starting it on the
188	// first connection. Each successful acquire must be paired with a release.
189	// Unlike changeHubRegistry.acquire, this can fail — the underlying NATS
190	// subscribe call can itself error (e.g. a permissions violation) — in which
191	// case no hub is registered, so a subsequent connection gets a fresh attempt
192	// rather than being stuck sharing a broken one.
193	func (r *refHubRegistry) acquire(repoID string) (*refHub, error) {
194		r.mu.Lock()
195		defer r.mu.Unlock()
196		if h := r.hubs[repoID]; h != nil {
197			h.refs++
198			return h, nil
199		}
200		// The hub's subscription must outlive whichever connection happens to
201		// create it, so it is subscribed under its OWN long-lived context, never
202		// the first caller's request context (cancelled the moment that caller
203		// disconnects, which must not tear down a subscription later callers are
204		// now also relying on).
205		hubCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
206		ch, unsub, err := r.subscribe(hubCtx, repoID)
207		if err != nil {
208			cancel()
209			return nil, err
210		}
211		h := newRefHub(repoID, ch, unsub, hubCtx, cancel)
212		if r.reconnected != nil {
213			h.reconnected, h.unwatch = r.reconnected()
214		}
215		r.hubs[repoID] = h
216		h.refs = 1
217		h.start()
218		return h, nil
219	}
220	
221	// release drops one reference to h; when the last connection leaves, the hub
222	// is removed from the registry and its subscription torn down. A fresh
223	// connection arriving concurrently takes r.mu, doesn't find the removed hub,
224	// and starts a new one — so a stopping hub is never handed out.
225	func (r *refHubRegistry) release(h *refHub) {
226		r.mu.Lock()
227		h.refs--
228		stop := h.refs <= 0
229		if stop {
230			delete(r.hubs, h.repoID)
231		}
232		r.mu.Unlock()
233		if stop {
234			h.stop()
235		}
236	}
237	
238	// refHub is one shared per-repo live ref-events drainer (per replica): it
239	// owns the repo's NATS subscription, debounces rapid updates to the same ref
240	// (refDebounceWindow), and fans each debounced event out to every connection
241	// watching the repo (filtered by that connection's own prefix set at
242	// delivery) — so N viewers of a hot repo cost one subscription, not N. Its
243	// subscription outlives any single request, running under its own context
244	// (cancelled by stop), never a request context.
245	type refHub struct {
246		repoID      string
247		sub         <-chan ingest.RefEvent
248		unsub       func()
249		ctx         context.Context
250		cancel      context.CancelFunc
251		done        chan struct{} // closed when the drain goroutine exits (stop waits on it)
252		reconnected <-chan nats.Status
253		unwatch     func()
254	
255		refs int // guarded by the owning registry's mu
256	
257		mu      sync.Mutex
258		conns   map[*refHubConn]struct{}
259		pending map[string]ingest.RefEvent // ref_name -> latest event awaiting its debounce flush; presence IS "a flush is already scheduled"
260	}
261	
262	func newRefHub(repoID string, sub <-chan ingest.RefEvent, unsub func(), ctx context.Context, cancel context.CancelFunc) *refHub {
263		return &refHub{
264			repoID: repoID, sub: sub, unsub: unsub, ctx: ctx, cancel: cancel,
265			done:    make(chan struct{}),
266			conns:   map[*refHubConn]struct{}{},
267			pending: map[string]ingest.RefEvent{},
268		}
269	}
270	
271	func (h *refHub) start() { go h.run() }
272	
273	// stop cancels the hub, tears down its NATS subscription, and waits for the
274	// drain goroutine to exit — so a released hub is fully quiesced before its
275	// slot is reused. Any debounce timer still pending at this point fires
276	// harmlessly afterward (within refDebounceWindow) and no-ops via flush's own
277	// h.ctx.Err() guard, so there's nothing further to cancel here.
278	func (h *refHub) stop() {
279		h.cancel()
280		h.unsub()
281		<-h.done
282		if h.unwatch != nil {
283			h.unwatch()
284		}
285	}
286	
287	// run drains the shared NATS subscription until the hub is stopped,
288	// debouncing each ref through scheduleFlush. Unlike the DB-polling hubs' run
289	// loop, there is no poll cadence or backoff here — delivery is purely
290	// event-driven off the channel refstream.Subscribe returns; refstream itself
291	// logs and drops anything it can't parse, so every value received here is a
292	// valid ingest.RefEvent.
293	func (h *refHub) run() {
294		defer close(h.done)
295		for {
296			select {
297			case <-h.ctx.Done():
298				return
299			case ev := <-h.sub:
300				h.scheduleFlush(ev)
301			case _, ok := <-h.reconnected:
302				if !ok {
303					h.reconnected = nil
304					continue
305				}
306				h.ring()
307			}
308		}
309	}
310	
311	// ring wakes every connection after a reconnect: what moved meanwhile was
312	// never published.
313	func (h *refHub) ring() {
314		h.mu.Lock()
315		defer h.mu.Unlock()
316		for c := range h.conns {
317			c.signal()
318		}
319	}
320	
321	// scheduleFlush implements the leaky-bucket debounce described at the top of
322	// this file: the first update to a quiet ref schedules flush() at most
323	// refDebounceWindow out; a further update to that same ref before the timer
324	// fires just replaces the pending payload without rescheduling, bounding the
325	// worst-case delivery latency for any single update to refDebounceWindow
326	// regardless of how hot the ref is. Whether a flush is already scheduled is
327	// read directly off h.pending (its presence for this ref IS the scheduled
328	// state) rather than a second timers map kept in lockstep with it. Doorbells
329	// are rung here, as the event arrives, and left out of the flush.
330	func (h *refHub) scheduleFlush(ev ingest.RefEvent) {
331		h.mu.Lock()
332		defer h.mu.Unlock()
333		for c := range h.conns {
334			if c.doorbell {
335				c.deliver(ev)
336			}
337		}
338		_, alreadyScheduled := h.pending[ev.RefName]
339		h.pending[ev.RefName] = ev
340		if alreadyScheduled {
341			return
342		}
343		refName := ev.RefName // captured alone, not ev, so the timer doesn't keep the whole event alive
344		time.AfterFunc(refDebounceWindow, func() { h.flush(refName) })
345	}
346	
347	// flush delivers the latest pending event for refName to every connection
348	// currently watching this hub and clears the debounce state for that ref.
349	// Delivery runs inside the same h.mu critical section as the pending-map
350	// read: refHubConn.deliver only ever takes its own c.mu, never h.mu, so this
351	// can't deadlock, and it avoids copying the connection set to a slice on
352	// every flush (this fires per distinct ref about every refDebounceWindow, not
353	// a rare event) at the cost of briefly serializing flush against
354	// add/remove/scheduleFlush.
355	func (h *refHub) flush(refName string) {
356		h.mu.Lock()
357		defer h.mu.Unlock()
358		if h.ctx.Err() != nil {
359			return // hub stopping/stopped; every connection is already gone or going
360		}
361		ev, ok := h.pending[refName]
362		delete(h.pending, refName)
363		if !ok {
364			return
365		}
366		for c := range h.conns {
367			if !c.doorbell {
368				c.deliver(ev)
369			}
370		}
371	}
372	
373	func (h *refHub) add(prefixes []string) *refHubConn { return h.join(prefixes, false) }
374	
375	// addDoorbell is add, rung as each event arrives rather than debounced (see the
376	// file header).
377	func (h *refHub) addDoorbell(prefixes []string) *refHubConn { return h.join(prefixes, true) }
378	
379	func (h *refHub) join(prefixes []string, doorbell bool) *refHubConn {
380		c := &refHubConn{prefixes: prefixes, doorbell: doorbell, pending: map[string]ingest.RefEvent{}, wake: make(chan struct{}, 1)}
381		h.mu.Lock()
382		h.conns[c] = struct{}{}
383		h.mu.Unlock()
384		return c
385	}
386	
387	func (h *refHub) remove(c *refHubConn) {
388		h.mu.Lock()
389		delete(h.conns, c)
390		h.mu.Unlock()
391	}
392	
393	// refHubConn is one connection's state within a refHub: its own prefix
394	// filter and a single-slot-per-ref mailbox of undelivered events. Because the
395	// hub already debounces each ref to "latest wins" before delivery, a
396	// connection never needs a growing queue — if it hasn't drained the previous
397	// delivery for a ref before a new one arrives, the mailbox just holds the
398	// newer one (still "latest wins", now applied per-connection too), so no
399	// separate backpressure/slow-consumer policy is needed beyond this map.
400	type refHubConn struct {
401		prefixes []string // nil/empty = every ref
402		doorbell bool     // delivered undebounced (addDoorbell)
403	
404		mu      sync.Mutex
405		pending map[string]ingest.RefEvent
406		wake    chan struct{} // buffered(1)
407	}
408	
409	func (c *refHubConn) signal() { signalWake(c.wake) }
410	
411	// matches reports whether refName passes this connection's prefix filter (no
412	// filter → everything) — the same prefix semantics as GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs.
413	func (c *refHubConn) matches(refName string) bool {
414		if len(c.prefixes) == 0 {
415			return true
416		}
417		for _, p := range c.prefixes {
418			if strings.HasPrefix(refName, p) {
419				return true
420			}
421		}
422		return false
423	}
424	
425	func (c *refHubConn) deliver(ev ingest.RefEvent) {
426		if !c.matches(ev.RefName) {
427			return
428		}
429		c.mu.Lock()
430		c.pending[ev.RefName] = ev
431		c.mu.Unlock()
432		c.signal()
433	}

435	// drain empties and returns the connection's pending mailbox, or nil without
436	// allocating a replacement map when it's already empty — called every
437	// ~1s tick from refConnLoop for every open connection, so an idle connection
438	// (the common case between debounce flushes) shouldn't cost an allocation.
439	// Ranging over a nil map is a no-op, so callers need no special case.
440	func (c *refHubConn) drain() map[string]ingest.RefEvent {
441		c.mu.Lock()
442		defer c.mu.Unlock()
443		if len(c.pending) == 0 {
444			return nil
445		}
446		batch := c.pending
447		c.pending = map[string]ingest.RefEvent{}
448		return batch
449	}
450	
451	// ---- per-connection stream ----
452	
453	// refEventsSnapshot fetches a connection's initial ref state — a live
454	// entiredb ListRefsWithSymrefs read (NOT repo_branch_tip, which only tracks
455	// branches and never resolves symref targets), filtered by the connection's
456	// own requested prefixes. symrefs=true so a HEAD entry's SymrefTarget
457	// (refSnapshotEntryJSON) is actually populated, matching what the field
458	// promises.
459	type refEventsSnapshot func(ctx context.Context, prefixes []string) ([]repoapi.RefEntry, error)

1	package httpapi
2	
3	// SSE (text/event-stream) live ref-change stream: GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs/events.
4	//
5	// Unlike the DB-polling SSE families (reviews_events_sse.go, threads_events_sse.go —
6	// one shared poll per resource, fanned out to every connection), this hub is
7	// push-driven: it owns one shared core NATS subscription per repo_id
8	// (internal/refstream, subject repo_refs_v1.{repo_id}), fed by entiredb's
9	// live ref-push stream, and fans debounced events out to every connection
10	// watching that repo — so N viewers of a hot repo cost one subscription, not
11	// N, the same "one shared drain" leverage as the poll-based hubs, just
12	// sourced from NATS instead of a store poll.
13	//
14	// Design, decided after exploring alternatives (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY was a
15	// lower-infra-cost option; not chosen because it was scoped for a
16	// low-latency signal at real scale):
17	//   - Source: a plain core (non-JetStream) NATS subscription, not a durable
18	//     JetStream consumer — at-most-once delivery is the right contract for a
19	//     live tail where a client re-syncs current state on every reconnect
20	//     rather than replaying history. See internal/refstream.
21	//   - Debounce: rapid updates to the SAME ref are coalesced to at most one
22	//     flush per refDebounceWindow (leaky-bucket: the first update schedules a
23	//     flush; further updates before it fires just replace the pending
24	//     payload, latest wins), computed ONCE in the hub and fanned out — so a
25	//     hot repo with many viewers doesn't multiply (raw update rate × viewer
26	//     count) into unbounded per-connection work. A doorbell (addDoorbell) is
27	//     rung at once instead: it renders no event, only reads what moved, and
28	//     its one-slot wake already folds a burst into the next read. The
29	//     debounce never merged across refs: each ref has its own timer, so a
30	//     burst over several refs flushed with the spacing it arrived with.
31	//   - No persisted history, no cursor, no catch-up walk (unlike the
32	//     poll-based hubs): this is a live-only signal. A connection's initial
33	//     state comes from a one-time live entiredb ListRefsWithSymrefs read (the
34	//     "snapshot" frame) — NOT repo_branch_tip, which only tracks branches
35	//     and never resolves symref targets — filtered by the same `prefix` the
36	//     connection requested, matching GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs's own
37	//     repeatable prefix convention (api/repov1.ListRefsInput, entiredb) so a
38	//     client that already knows that filter gets it for free here. symrefs=true
39	//     so a HEAD entry's symrefTarget is actually populated in the snapshot.
40	//   - Re-auth: unlike a poll-driven hub (which gets re-auth "for free" every
41	//     poll tick), a push-driven connection has no natural tick — a quiet
42	//     repo could go minutes between NATS messages — so each connection runs
43	//     its own ~ssePollInterval re-auth timer via the same shared
44	//     cachedStreamAuth cache the poll-based hubs use.
45	import (
46		"context"
47		"errors"
48		"net/http"
49		"strings"
50		"sync"
51		"time"
52	
53		"github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2"
54		"github.com/entirehq/entiredb/modules/apidocs"
55		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
56	
57		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/ingest"
58		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/refstream"
59		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/repoapi"
60	)
61	
62	// refDebounceWindow bounds how long a burst of rapid updates to the SAME ref
63	// can be coalesced into one delivered event: the first update to a quiet ref
64	// schedules a flush at most this far out; any further update to that ref
65	// before the flush fires just replaces the pending payload (latest wins)
66	// instead of rescheduling the timer, so a continuously hot ref still flushes
67	// on a steady ~refDebounceWindow cadence rather than waiting for a quiet
68	// moment that never comes. A package var (not a const), matching
69	// ssePollInterval et al. in reviews_events_sse.go, so a test can shrink it to
70	// run in milliseconds.
71	var refDebounceWindow = 200 * time.Millisecond
72	
73	// RefEventsInput is GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs/events.
74	type RefEventsInput struct {
75		RepoID string `path:"repo_id"`
76		// Prefix mirrors GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs's own repeatable prefix filter
77		// verbatim (api/repov1.ListRefsInput, entiredb): query:"prefix,explode",
78		// maxItems 100, empty = every ref.
79		Prefix []string `query:"prefix,explode" maxItems:"100" doc:"Ref-name prefixes to filter by (repeatable), e.g. \"refs/heads/\", \"refs/tags/\", \"HEAD\" — the same convention as GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs. Empty streams every ref."`
80	}
81	
82	// refSnapshotEntryJSON/refSnapshotData/refDeltaData are the SSE payloads,
83	// camelCase per CASING-001 (matching toReviewEventJSON/toThreadEventJSON).
84	
85	type refSnapshotEntryJSON struct {
86		Name         string `json:"name"`
87		OID          string `json:"oid,omitempty"`
88		SymrefTarget string `json:"symrefTarget,omitempty"`
89	}
90	
91	type refSnapshotData struct {
92		Refs []refSnapshotEntryJSON `json:"refs"`
93	}
94	
95	// refDeltaData is one live ref-change event, projected from ingest.RefEvent.
96	// The SSE `event:` name is normally the ref op itself (create/update/
97	// force_update/delete/symref_update — entiredb's refevents.RefOp* wire
98	// values), mirroring the review/thread hubs' convention of using the event's
99	// own type as the frame name — but see refFrameEvent for why the frame name
100	// is validated first. RefOp is also carried in the JSON body regardless, so a
101	// client can always recover the real op even on the rare refFallbackOp path.
102	type refDeltaData struct {
103		RefName         string `json:"refName"`
104		RefOp           string `json:"refOp"`
105		OldTarget       string `json:"oldTarget,omitempty"`
106		NewTarget       string `json:"newTarget,omitempty"`
107		OldSymrefTarget string `json:"oldSymrefTarget,omitempty"`
108		NewSymrefTarget string `json:"newSymrefTarget,omitempty"`
109		PusherID        string `json:"pusherId,omitempty"`
110		EventAt         string `json:"eventAt"`
111	}
112	
113	func toRefDeltaData(ev ingest.RefEvent) refDeltaData {
114		return refDeltaData{
115			RefName:         ev.RefName,
116			RefOp:           ev.RefOp,
117			OldTarget:       ev.OldTarget,
118			NewTarget:       ev.NewTarget,
119			OldSymrefTarget: ev.OldSymrefTarget,
120			NewSymrefTarget: ev.NewSymrefTarget,
121			PusherID:        ev.PusherID,
122			EventAt:         isoMillis(ev.Timestamp),
123		}
124	}
125	
126	// refKnownOps is the closed set of ref_op wire values entiredb's envelope
127	// version 1 ever publishes on repo_refs_v1 (refevents.RefOp{Create,Update,
128	// Delete,ForceUpdate}, plus internal/ingest's own unexported
129	// refOpSymrefUpdate — both mirrored here as literals since neither package
130	// exports them for this use).
131	var refKnownOps = map[string]bool{
132		"create": true, "update": true, "delete": true, "force_update": true,
133		"symref_update": true,
134	}
135	
136	// refFallbackOp substitutes for any ref_op outside refKnownOps.
137	const refFallbackOp = "ref_change"
138	
139	// refFrameEvent returns refOp verbatim if it's one of refKnownOps, else
140	// refFallbackOp. ev.RefOp is decoded straight from an external NATS payload
141	// with no format check (ingest.ParseRefEvent), and sseWriter.frame
142	// (reviews_events_sse.go) builds a frame by raw string concatenation with no
143	// escaping — unlike the DB-polling hubs, whose event: name always comes from
144	// an internal, store-constrained enum. Without this check, a ref_op
145	// containing "\n"/"\r" would inject extra lines into the frame, corrupting it
146	// for every connection sharing that repo's hub. The real value is never lost
147	// even on the fallback path — refDeltaData.RefOp (JSON-escaped, so safe
148	// regardless of its content) always carries it too.
149	func refFrameEvent(refOp string) string {
150		if refKnownOps[refOp] {
151			return refOp
152		}
153		return refFallbackOp
154	}
155	
156	// ---- shared per-repo push drain ----
157	
158	// refEventHubs is shared so a repo costs one NATS subscription per replica.
159	func (deps *RepoActivityDeps) refEventHubs() *refHubRegistry {
160		deps.refHubsOnce.Do(func() {
161			deps.refHubs = newRefHubRegistry(func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error) {
162				return refstream.Subscribe(ctx, deps.RefEventsNATS, repoID)
163			})
164			deps.refHubs.reconnected = func() (<-chan nats.Status, func()) {
165				return refstream.Reconnected(deps.RefEventsNATS)
166			}
167		})
168		return deps.refHubs
169	}
170	
171	// refHubRegistry maps a repo_id to its live per-replica ref-events hub,
172	// ref-counted so a hub is created (and subscribed) on the first connection
173	// and torn down when the last leaves — the push-driven counterpart of
174	// changeHubRegistry (reviews_events_sse.go): one shared NATS subscription per
175	// repo, never one per connection.
176	type refHubRegistry struct {
177		mu          sync.Mutex
178		hubs        map[string]*refHub
179		subscribe   func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error)
180		reconnected func() (<-chan nats.Status, func())
181	}
182	
183	func newRefHubRegistry(subscribe func(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (<-chan ingest.RefEvent, func(), error)) *refHubRegistry {
184		return &refHubRegistry{hubs: map[string]*refHub{}, subscribe: subscribe}
185	}
186	
187	// acquire returns the live hub for repoID, subscribing and starting it on the
188	// first connection. Each successful acquire must be paired with a release.
189	// Unlike changeHubRegistry.acquire, this can fail — the underlying NATS
190	// subscribe call can itself error (e.g. a permissions violation) — in which
191	// case no hub is registered, so a subsequent connection gets a fresh attempt
192	// rather than being stuck sharing a broken one.
193	func (r *refHubRegistry) acquire(repoID string) (*refHub, error) {
194		r.mu.Lock()
195		defer r.mu.Unlock()
196		if h := r.hubs[repoID]; h != nil {
197			h.refs++
198			return h, nil
199		}
200		// The hub's subscription must outlive whichever connection happens to
201		// create it, so it is subscribed under its OWN long-lived context, never
202		// the first caller's request context (cancelled the moment that caller
203		// disconnects, which must not tear down a subscription later callers are
204		// now also relying on).
205		hubCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
206		ch, unsub, err := r.subscribe(hubCtx, repoID)
207		if err != nil {
208			cancel()
209			return nil, err
210		}
211		h := newRefHub(repoID, ch, unsub, hubCtx, cancel)
212		if r.reconnected != nil {
213			h.reconnected, h.unwatch = r.reconnected()
214		}
215		r.hubs[repoID] = h
216		h.refs = 1
217		h.start()
218		return h, nil
219	}
220	
221	// release drops one reference to h; when the last connection leaves, the hub
222	// is removed from the registry and its subscription torn down. A fresh
223	// connection arriving concurrently takes r.mu, doesn't find the removed hub,
224	// and starts a new one — so a stopping hub is never handed out.
225	func (r *refHubRegistry) release(h *refHub) {
226		r.mu.Lock()
227		h.refs--
228		stop := h.refs <= 0
229		if stop {
230			delete(r.hubs, h.repoID)
231		}
232		r.mu.Unlock()
233		if stop {
234			h.stop()
235		}
236	}
237	
238	// refHub is one shared per-repo live ref-events drainer (per replica): it
239	// owns the repo's NATS subscription, debounces rapid updates to the same ref
240	// (refDebounceWindow), and fans each debounced event out to every connection
241	// watching the repo (filtered by that connection's own prefix set at
242	// delivery) — so N viewers of a hot repo cost one subscription, not N. Its
243	// subscription outlives any single request, running under its own context
244	// (cancelled by stop), never a request context.
245	type refHub struct {
246		repoID      string
247		sub         <-chan ingest.RefEvent
248		unsub       func()
249		ctx         context.Context
250		cancel      context.CancelFunc
251		done        chan struct{} // closed when the drain goroutine exits (stop waits on it)
252		reconnected <-chan nats.Status
253		unwatch     func()
254	
255		refs int // guarded by the owning registry's mu
256	
257		mu      sync.Mutex
258		conns   map[*refHubConn]struct{}
259		pending map[string]ingest.RefEvent // ref_name -> latest event awaiting its debounce flush; presence IS "a flush is already scheduled"
260	}
261	
262	func newRefHub(repoID string, sub <-chan ingest.RefEvent, unsub func(), ctx context.Context, cancel context.CancelFunc) *refHub {
263		return &refHub{
264			repoID: repoID, sub: sub, unsub: unsub, ctx: ctx, cancel: cancel,
265			done:    make(chan struct{}),
266			conns:   map[*refHubConn]struct{}{},
267			pending: map[string]ingest.RefEvent{},
268		}
269	}
270	
271	func (h *refHub) start() { go h.run() }
272	
273	// stop cancels the hub, tears down its NATS subscription, and waits for the
274	// drain goroutine to exit — so a released hub is fully quiesced before its
275	// slot is reused. Any debounce timer still pending at this point fires
276	// harmlessly afterward (within refDebounceWindow) and no-ops via flush's own
277	// h.ctx.Err() guard, so there's nothing further to cancel here.
278	func (h *refHub) stop() {
279		h.cancel()
280		h.unsub()
281		<-h.done
282		if h.unwatch != nil {
283			h.unwatch()
284		}
285	}
286	
287	// run drains the shared NATS subscription until the hub is stopped,
288	// debouncing each ref through scheduleFlush. Unlike the DB-polling hubs' run
289	// loop, there is no poll cadence or backoff here — delivery is purely
290	// event-driven off the channel refstream.Subscribe returns; refstream itself
291	// logs and drops anything it can't parse, so every value received here is a
292	// valid ingest.RefEvent.
293	func (h *refHub) run() {
294		defer close(h.done)
295		for {
296			select {
297			case <-h.ctx.Done():
298				return
299			case ev := <-h.sub:
300				h.scheduleFlush(ev)
301			case _, ok := <-h.reconnected:
302				if !ok {
303					h.reconnected = nil
304					continue
305				}
306				h.ring()
307			}
308		}
309	}
310	
311	// ring wakes every connection after a reconnect: what moved meanwhile was
312	// never published.
313	func (h *refHub) ring() {
314		h.mu.Lock()
315		defer h.mu.Unlock()
316		for c := range h.conns {
317			c.signal()
318		}
319	}
320	
321	// scheduleFlush implements the leaky-bucket debounce described at the top of
322	// this file: the first update to a quiet ref schedules flush() at most
323	// refDebounceWindow out; a further update to that same ref before the timer
324	// fires just replaces the pending payload without rescheduling, bounding the
325	// worst-case delivery latency for any single update to refDebounceWindow
326	// regardless of how hot the ref is. Whether a flush is already scheduled is
327	// read directly off h.pending (its presence for this ref IS the scheduled
328	// state) rather than a second timers map kept in lockstep with it. Doorbells
329	// are rung here, as the event arrives, and left out of the flush.
330	func (h *refHub) scheduleFlush(ev ingest.RefEvent) {
331		h.mu.Lock()
332		defer h.mu.Unlock()
333		for c := range h.conns {
334			if c.doorbell {
335				c.deliver(ev)
336			}
337		}
338		_, alreadyScheduled := h.pending[ev.RefName]
339		h.pending[ev.RefName] = ev
340		if alreadyScheduled {
341			return
342		}
343		refName := ev.RefName // captured alone, not ev, so the timer doesn't keep the whole event alive
344		time.AfterFunc(refDebounceWindow, func() { h.flush(refName) })
345	}
346	
347	// flush delivers the latest pending event for refName to every connection
348	// currently watching this hub and clears the debounce state for that ref.
349	// Delivery runs inside the same h.mu critical section as the pending-map
350	// read: refHubConn.deliver only ever takes its own c.mu, never h.mu, so this
351	// can't deadlock, and it avoids copying the connection set to a slice on
352	// every flush (this fires per distinct ref about every refDebounceWindow, not
353	// a rare event) at the cost of briefly serializing flush against
354	// add/remove/scheduleFlush.
355	func (h *refHub) flush(refName string) {
356		h.mu.Lock()
357		defer h.mu.Unlock()
358		if h.ctx.Err() != nil {
359			return // hub stopping/stopped; every connection is already gone or going
360		}
361		ev, ok := h.pending[refName]
362		delete(h.pending, refName)
363		if !ok {
364			return
365		}
366		for c := range h.conns {
367			if !c.doorbell {
368				c.deliver(ev)
369			}
370		}
371	}
372	
373	func (h *refHub) add(prefixes []string) *refHubConn { return h.join(prefixes, false) }
374	
375	// addDoorbell is add, rung as each event arrives rather than debounced (see the
376	// file header).
377	func (h *refHub) addDoorbell(prefixes []string) *refHubConn { return h.join(prefixes, true) }
378	
379	func (h *refHub) join(prefixes []string, doorbell bool) *refHubConn {
380		c := &refHubConn{prefixes: prefixes, doorbell: doorbell, pending: map[string]ingest.RefEvent{}, wake: make(chan struct{}, 1)}
381		h.mu.Lock()
382		h.conns[c] = struct{}{}
383		h.mu.Unlock()
384		return c
385	}
386	
387	func (h *refHub) remove(c *refHubConn) {
388		h.mu.Lock()
389		delete(h.conns, c)
390		h.mu.Unlock()
391	}
392	
393	// refHubConn is one connection's state within a refHub: its own prefix
394	// filter and a single-slot-per-ref mailbox of undelivered events. Because the
395	// hub already debounces each ref to "latest wins" before delivery, a
396	// connection never needs a growing queue — if it hasn't drained the previous
397	// delivery for a ref before a new one arrives, the mailbox just holds the
398	// newer one (still "latest wins", now applied per-connection too), so no
399	// separate backpressure/slow-consumer policy is needed beyond this map.
400	type refHubConn struct {
401		prefixes []string // nil/empty = every ref
402		doorbell bool     // delivered undebounced (addDoorbell)
403	
404		mu      sync.Mutex
405		pending map[string]ingest.RefEvent
406		wake    chan struct{} // buffered(1)
407	}
408	
409	func (c *refHubConn) signal() { signalWake(c.wake) }
410	
411	// matches reports whether refName passes this connection's prefix filter (no
412	// filter → everything) — the same prefix semantics as GET /repos/{repo_id}/refs.
413	func (c *refHubConn) matches(refName string) bool {
414		if len(c.prefixes) == 0 {
415			return true
416		}
417		for _, p := range c.prefixes {
418			if strings.HasPrefix(refName, p) {
419				return true
420			}
421		}
422		return false
423	}
424	
425	func (c *refHubConn) deliver(ev ingest.RefEvent) {
426		if !c.matches(ev.RefName) {
427			return
428		}
429		c.mu.Lock()
430		c.pending[ev.RefName] = ev
431		c.mu.Unlock()
432		c.signal()
433	}
434	
435	// drain empties and returns the connection's pending mailbox, or nil without
436	// allocating a replacement map when it's already empty — called every
437	// ~1s tick from refConnLoop for every open connection, so an idle connection
438	// (the common case between debounce flushes) shouldn't cost an allocation.
439	// Ranging over a nil map is a no-op, so callers need no special case.
440	func (c *refHubConn) drain() map[string]ingest.RefEvent {
441		c.mu.Lock()
442		defer c.mu.Unlock()
443		if len(c.pending) == 0 {
444			return nil
445		}
446		batch := c.pending
447		c.pending = map[string]ingest.RefEvent{}
448		return batch
449	}
450	
451	// ---- per-connection stream ----
452	
453	// refEventsSnapshot fetches a connection's initial ref state — a live
454	// entiredb ListRefsWithSymrefs read (NOT repo_branch_tip, which only tracks
455	// branches and never resolves symref targets), filtered by the connection's
456	// own requested prefixes. symrefs=true so a HEAD entry's SymrefTarget
457	// (refSnapshotEntryJSON) is actually populated, matching what the field
458	// promises.
459	type refEventsSnapshot func(ctx context.Context, prefixes []string) ([]repoapi.RefEntry, error)
460
