1	// Package authz decides whether a push may touch the refs it names.
2	//
3	// Write access to a repository is push access to every store in it. Nothing in
4	// the record protocol changes that: a store's refs are ordinary refs and git has
5	// no per-ref authorization. So the boundary a group actually gets is whatever the
6	// server enforces at receive time, and this package is the decision that
7	// enforcement makes — a pure function of a policy, an identity and the ref
8	// updates a push proposes.
9	//
10	// It is deliberately not a signing scheme. Signatures answer "who wrote this
11	// value", survive compaction, and are checked by readers; that lives on the
12	// record and outside the protocol. This answers "who may move this ref", is
13	// checked once at push time by the server, and protects the parts of the layout
14	// that no later reader could tell had been tampered with.
15	package authz
16	
17	import (
18		"fmt"
19		"sort"
20		"strconv"
21		"strings"
22	
23		"github.com/entirehq/strata/reflayout"
24	)
25	
26	// Update is one line of what a push proposes: a ref, what the server holds, and
27	// what the push would leave there. Old is all zeros for a creation and New is all
28	// zeros for a deletion, which is git's own convention on a hook's stdin.
29	type Update struct {
30		Ref string
31		Old string
32		New string
33	}
34	
35	// Creating reports whether the ref does not exist on the server yet.

37

75	// this layout wants is a prefix — but which a *breadth* of pattern does. Granting

104		pattern string

111	// diff of it. A format that needs a tool to see what changed is a format where a
112	// grant slips through review.

122			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
123			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
124				continue
125			}

127			if len(fields) != 3 {
128				return nil, fmt.Errorf("authz: line %d: want \"<rule> <identity> <ref-pattern>\", got %q", n+1, line)

225	//

241	// pre-receive runs once per push and sees every ref it proposes. So this stays a
242	// pure function with no git in it, like everything else here.
243	func oneShotWriters(updates []Update) map[string]bool {
244		type parts struct {

246			extra                      bool

248		seen := map[string]*parts{}

267			case r.Kind == reflayout.LogRotation && r.Rotation == 0:
268				p.log = true
269			case r.Kind == reflayout.Evicted:
270				p.evicted = true
271			default:

273			}
274		}
275		out := map[string]bool{}
276		for key, p := range seen {
277			if p.announcement && p.log && p.evicted && !p.extra {
278				out[key] = true
279			}
280		}
281		return out

285	func (p *Policy) introduces(identity, store string) bool {

294	// Check returns every update the identity may not make.

321		return out
322	}

324	func (p *Policy) permits(identity, ref string, way direction) bool {
325		for _, r := range p.allow[identity] {

338		}
339		return false
340	}

342	// rules are the words a policy line may begin with.
343	//
344	// Two directions and not three. Nothing in this design wants update-only: a
345	// writer needs every direction on its own refs, and an operator needs create and
346	// delete on other writers'. A third word would be one no generator emits, and
347	// Parse refuses what it does not know — so the day something wants it, adding it
348	// is a line here rather than a gap nobody noticed.

350		"allow":        anyDirection,
351		"allow-create": creating,
352		"allow-delete": deleting,
353		// allow-oneshot is a different kind of rule and carries no direction of its
354		// own: what it permits is a whole writer arriving at once, which is three
355		// creations or nothing. See oneShotWriters.
356		"allow-oneshot": 0,
357	}
358	
359	func ruleWords() string {
360		words := make([]string, 0, len(rules))
361		for w := range rules {
362			words = append(words, strconv.Quote(w))
363		}
364		sort.Strings(words)
365		return strings.Join(words, ", ")
366	}

368	// shapeOf returns why the layout forbids an update, or "" if it does not.
369	//
370	// The layout itself is reflayout's; what may be *done* to a ref it describes is
371	// this package's, and that is the whole of the split. A generation is the one
372	// shape with a rule beyond its name, and the rule is about object ids — which
373	// reflayout has never heard of and should not.
374	func shapeOf(u Update) string {
375		r := reflayout.Parse(u.Ref)
376		if reason := r.Refusal(); reason != "" {
377			return reason
378		}
379		// A generation is verified by recomputation, which only works while the
380		// bytes at a number are the bytes everyone folded. Replacing them leaves
381		// no evidence in any later read: a clone that had already adopted the old
382		// generation is simply, permanently, holding different data from one that
383		// adopts the new one. Creating and deleting are how generations are meant
384		// to move — published once, dropped by retention — and neither can do
385		// that.
386		if r.Kind == reflayout.Gen && !u.Creating() && !u.Deleting() {
387			return "a published generation cannot be replaced"
388		}
389		return ""
390	}

205	// permanent divergence. So no grant can name it, and until this existed a CI
206	// runner could report to a store nobody guarded and to no other kind.
207	//
208	// This names the shape instead. The glossary already defines a one-shot writer
209	// as one that "creates its log, writes once, never appends, and evicts itself
210	// on completion", and that sentence is the whole of what this permits:
211	// announcement, log at rotation zero, and eviction, arriving together as
212	// creations for one writer.
213	//
214	// The pattern names the store and carries no "/*", because this rule does not
215	// match a ref by prefix and a wildcard would suggest it does.
216	func OneShot(identity, store string) []string { return []string{OneShotLine(identity, store)} }
217	
218	// OneShotLine is the single line OneShot returns, for a caller composing a policy
219	// by hand rather than joining slices.
220	func OneShotLine(identity, store string) string {
221		return fmt.Sprintf("allow-oneshot %s %s", identity, reflayout.For(store).Root().Prefix())
222	}
223	
224	// oneShotWriters returns the writers this push introduces whole.
225	//
226	// A writer qualifies only if the push creates its low-water mark, its log at
227	// rotation zero, and its eviction — all three, all as creations, and nothing else
228	// of its. Everything that makes the grant safe falls out of that rather than
229	// being checked separately:
230	//
231	//   - It cannot be grafted onto a writer that already exists, because that
232	//     writer's announcement is already there, so the update naming it would
233	//     not be a creation and the set would be short.
234	//   - It cannot append later, because rotation zero is named and a second push
235	//     carrying one ref is not a whole writer.
236	//   - It cannot introduce a writer that does not close itself, because the
237	//     eviction is one of the three. A writer arriving without one would count
238	//     toward the barrier for ever, and there is no clone left to evict it.
239	//
240	// Decided from the update set alone, which the hook hands over whole: a
241	// pre-receive runs once per push and sees every ref it proposes. So this stays a
242	// pure function with no git in it, like everything else here.
243	func oneShotWriters(updates []Update) map[string]bool {
244		type parts struct {
245			announcement, log, evicted bool
246			extra                      bool
247		}
248		seen := map[string]*parts{}
249		for _, u := range updates {
250			r := reflayout.Parse(u.Ref)
251			if r.Writer == "" {
252				continue
253			}
254			key := r.Store + "\x00" + r.Writer
255			p := seen[key]
256			if p == nil {
257				p = &parts{}
258				seen[key] = p
259			}
260			if !u.Creating() {
261				p.extra = true
262				continue
263			}
264			switch {
265			case r.Kind == reflayout.Announcement:
266				p.announcement = true
267			case r.Kind == reflayout.LogRotation && r.Rotation == 0:
268				p.log = true
269			case r.Kind == reflayout.Evicted:
270				p.evicted = true
271			default:
272				p.extra = true
273			}
274		}
275		out := map[string]bool{}
276		for key, p := range seen {
277			if p.announcement && p.log && p.evicted && !p.extra {
278				out[key] = true
279			}
280		}
281		return out
282	}
283	
284	// introduces reports whether identity may introduce writers into ref's store.
285	func (p *Policy) introduces(identity, store string) bool {
286		for _, r := range p.allow[identity] {
287			if r.allows == 0 && r.pattern == reflayout.For(store).Root().Prefix() {
288				return true
289			}
290		}
291		return false
292	}
293	
294	// Check returns every update the identity may not make.
295	//
296	// Two things have to hold, and they are different in kind. The policy has to
297	// permit the ref, which is a deployment's decision. And the update has to be one
298	// the layout allows at all, which is the protocol's and applies to everyone —
299	// including an identity the policy trusts completely.
300	func (p *Policy) Check(identity string, updates []Update) []Rejection {
301		// Which writers this push introduces whole, decided once for the batch: a
302		// one-shot writer cannot be authorised a ref at a time, because what makes it
303		// safe to admit is the shape of the whole set.
304		whole := oneShotWriters(updates)
305	
306		var out []Rejection
307		for _, u := range updates {
308			if reason := shapeOf(u); reason != "" {
309				out = append(out, Rejection{u.Ref, reason})
310				continue
311			}
312			if p.permits(identity, u.Ref, directionOf(u)) {
313				continue
314			}
315			if r := reflayout.Parse(u.Ref); r.Writer != "" &&
316				whole[r.Store+"\x00"+r.Writer] && p.introduces(identity, r.Store) {
317				continue
318			}
319			out = append(out, Rejection{u.Ref, identity + " is not allowed to write this ref"})
320		}
321		return out
322	}
323	
324	func (p *Policy) permits(identity, ref string, way direction) bool {
325		for _, r := range p.allow[identity] {
326			if r.allows&way == 0 {
327				continue
328			}
329			if prefix, ok := strings.CutSuffix(r.pattern, "/*"); ok {
330				if strings.HasPrefix(ref, prefix+"/") {
331					return true
332				}
333				continue
334			}
335			if ref == r.pattern {
336				return true
337			}
338		}
339		return false
340	}
341	
342	// rules are the words a policy line may begin with.
343	//
344	// Two directions and not three. Nothing in this design wants update-only: a
345	// writer needs every direction on its own refs, and an operator needs create and
346	// delete on other writers'. A third word would be one no generator emits, and
347	// Parse refuses what it does not know — so the day something wants it, adding it
348	// is a line here rather than a gap nobody noticed.
349	var rules = map[string]direction{
350		"allow":        anyDirection,
351		"allow-create": creating,
352		"allow-delete": deleting,
353		// allow-oneshot is a different kind of rule and carries no direction of its
354		// own: what it permits is a whole writer arriving at once, which is three
355		// creations or nothing. See oneShotWriters.
356		"allow-oneshot": 0,
357	}
358	
359	func ruleWords() string {
360		words := make([]string, 0, len(rules))
361		for w := range rules {
362			words = append(words, strconv.Quote(w))
363		}
364		sort.Strings(words)
365		return strings.Join(words, ", ")
366	}
367	
368	// shapeOf returns why the layout forbids an update, or "" if it does not.
369	//
370	// The layout itself is reflayout's; what may be *done* to a ref it describes is
371	// this package's, and that is the whole of the split. A generation is the one
372	// shape with a rule beyond its name, and the rule is about object ids — which
373	// reflayout has never heard of and should not.
374	func shapeOf(u Update) string {
375		r := reflayout.Parse(u.Ref)
376		if reason := r.Refusal(); reason != "" {
377			return reason
378		}
379		// A generation is verified by recomputation, which only works while the
380		// bytes at a number are the bytes everyone folded. Replacing them leaves
381		// no evidence in any later read: a clone that had already adopted the old
382		// generation is simply, permanently, holding different data from one that
383		// adopts the new one. Creating and deleting are how generations are meant
384		// to move — published once, dropped by retention — and neither can do
385		// that.
386		if r.Kind == reflayout.Gen && !u.Creating() && !u.Deleting() {
387			return "a published generation cannot be replaced"
388		}
389		return ""
390	}

212	func (s *Service) HandleReceivePack(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, st *storage.Storage, pushSizeLimit int64, mirrorTargets *mirrorWriteTargets, mirrorRepo bool, protection *repostore.BranchProtection) {
213		ctx := r.Context()
214		ctx, span := otel.Tracer().Start(ctx, "server.handleReceivePack")
215		defer span.End()
216	
217		ctx = gitspan.WithRoot(ctx, span)
218		gitspan.SetOp(ctx, gitspan.OpPush)
219		gitspan.SetClientKindFromUA(ctx, r.Header.Get("User-Agent"))
220

264						slog.Uint64("threshold_bytes", threshold))

272		// Set response headers (matching go-git's serviceRPC pattern)
273		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/x-git-receive-pack-result")

282		// keep-alive connection. The constant lives in diss, next to the
283		// quarantine sweep grace that must stay strictly above it.
284		deadline := time.Now().Add(diss.PackfileIngestDeadline)

287			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: set read deadline", slog.Any("error", err))
288		}

290			if err := rc.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{}); err != nil {
291				slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: clear read deadline", slog.Any("error", err))
292			}
293		}()

295		defer cancel()

297		splitLOP := s.shouldSplitLOP(ctx, st)
298		limitWriter := w
299		if splitLOP {
300			limitWriter = bodyLimitWriter{w}

303		// Gate 2: MaxBytesReader safety net on the raw HTTP body.
304		// Catches tampered headers or clients that don't send X-Entire-Push-Size.
305		body := r.Body
306		if pushSizeLimit > 0 {
307			body = http.MaxBytesReader(limitWriter, r.Body, pushSizeLimit)
308		}

310		// Count wire (compressed) bytes for push.bytes_received telemetry.
311		// Wraps body BEFORE the gzip layer so the attribute records what the
312		// client actually sent over the wire, not the decompressed size. The
313		// final value is recorded via defer so every return path reports it.
314		bodyCounter := &countingReader{r: body}
315		body = struct {
316			io.Reader
317			io.Closer
318		}{Reader: bodyCounter, Closer: body}
319		defer func() { gitspan.SetPushBytesReceived(ctx, bodyCounter.n) }()

321		// Handle gzip content encoding
322		var reader io.ReadCloser
323		switch r.Header.Get("Content-Encoding") {
324		case compressionGzip:
325			gr, err := gzip.NewReader(body)

329				return
330			}
331			defer gr.Close()

333			// bytes can inflate past pushSizeLimit and let the parser see far

344		rd := bufio.NewReader(reader)

346		// Check for empty push (flush packet = client has nothing to send)

350			// packet. A zero-byte or truncated body (EOF before any pkt-line)

352			// source is a helper retry after a push that already landed.
353			// Answer 400, not 500: it's the honest status, it stops paging

388		}

390		for _, cmd := range updreq.Commands {
391			if gitwire.CommandAction(cmd) == packp.Invalid {

395		}

397		// Reject pathological ref names (path traversal, control chars, @{,

399		for _, cmd := range updreq.Commands {
400			if err := validatePushRefName(cmd.Name); err != nil {
401				slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: invalid ref name",
402					slog.String("ref", cmd.Name.String()),
403					slog.Any("error", err))

407			}
408		}

410		// Reject duplicate commands for the same ref (as C git receive-pack does).
411		// Everything downstream — CAS results, report-status, ref events, RSL —
412		// keys per-ref state by name, so duplicates would let one command's
413		// outcome silently mask the other's and the reported state could disagree
414		// with what was committed.
415		seenRefs := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]struct{}, len(updreq.Commands))
416		for _, cmd := range updreq.Commands {
417			if _, dup := seenRefs[cmd.Name]; dup {
418				slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: duplicate ref-update command",
419					slog.String("ref", cmd.Name.String()))

422				return
423			}

427		// Classify push shape and record span attributes.
428		var creates, updates, deletes int
429		for _, c := range updreq.Commands {
430			switch {
431			case c.Old.IsZero() && !c.New.IsZero():
432				creates++
433			case !c.Old.IsZero() && c.New.IsZero():
434				deletes++
435			default:
436				updates++
437			}

445			attribute.Int("push.delete_count", deletes),

449		var pushOptions []string

452			if err := pushOpts.Decode(rd); err != nil {

460		// The write path goes on the storer here, before the CAS transaction

474		// Build a flushing progress writer whenever there is a side-band to write

479		// scripted and CI pushes that rely on reading them back.

482			rc := http.NewResponseController(w)
483			if err := rc.EnableFullDuplex(); err != nil {

487			pw := &progressWriter{mux: mux, quiet: !wantProgress}

502		// Reject pushes to reserved ref namespaces (refs/internal/*, refs/replace/*,

504		//   - restore mode: entire-backup repopulates every ref a live cluster
505		//     carried, so the whole gate is skipped.
506		//   - a workload-writable namespace (namespaceWriters): a ref whose

519		// A native-mirror replication push is refused PER REF instead of whole
520		// (ENT-2423). It is a full-refset transfer that no operator drives, so one

523		// next attempt repeats it. Every other push stays all-or-nothing: a person

534				}

538					secsignal.WithSurface("githttp"),
539					secsignal.WithReason("reserved_ref"),
540					secsignal.WithResource("repo", st.RepoID().String()),
541					secsignal.WithDetail("security.detail.ref", cmd.Name.String()))

543					http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("push to %s is not allowed", cmd.Name), http.StatusForbidden)

545				}

558		// Refuse creating a branch whose whole name is a full-length object ID.
559		// Per ref, so an import that carries one still lands the rest.

562		// Writer scope: on a GitHub mirror, a worker sync may only write the

567		// Branch protection, applied here rather than left to AdvanceRefs (which
568		// enforces the same policy for every mirror write) for two reasons: a
569		// protected ref never reaches the packfile ingest below, and its refusal

574		//
575		// Two rules share this block, and the ref decides which one owns a

592			nativePolicy = refprotect.Policy{Protected: protection.Refs(), ServerSideMergeOnly: protection.ServerSideMergeOnlyRefs()}
593		}
594		var protectedErrors map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error
595		if len(mirrorRuleCmds) > 0 || len(nativeRuleCmds) > 0 {
596			protected := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error)
597			var err error
598			if len(mirrorRuleCmds) > 0 {
599				var refused map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error
600				refused, err = mirrorProtectedErrors(ctx, st, mirrorRuleCmds)

602			}
603			if err == nil && len(nativeRuleCmds) > 0 {
604				var refused map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error
605				refused, err = nativeProtectedErrors(ctx, st, nativePolicy, nativeRuleCmds, refprotect.Write{})
606				maps.Copy(protected, refused)
607			}
608			if err != nil {
609				// Policy evaluation failed before the packfile was read or any
610				// object work started — bail out cleanly rather than proceed as
611				// if nothing were protected. Reachable: refprotect.DefaultBranchSource

619				if _, drainErr := io.Copy(io.Discard, rd); drainErr != nil {
620					slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: draining unread packfile body", slog.Any("error", drainErr))

622				slogutil.Error(ctx, "receive-pack: branch protection check failed", slog.Any("error", err))
623				http.Error(w, "unable to evaluate branch protection", http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
624				return
625			}
626			for ref, refusal := range protected {
627				if protectedErrors == nil {
628					protectedErrors = make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error, 1)
629				}
630				protectedErrors[ref] = refusal
631				slogutil.Info(ctx, "receive-pack: rejecting write to protected ref",
632					slog.String("repo_id", st.RepoID().String()),
633					slog.String("ref", ref.String()))

637		// Create commands that would form a directory/file conflict with an
638		// existing ref (or another ref created earlier in the same batch) are
639		// rejected by the refstore CAS itself: the Create INSERT guards against
640		// the conflict and a hit surfaces as a per-ref refstore.ErrDirFileConflict

647		// reservedErrors cannot overlap protectedErrors: a reserved ref is not

660		namespaceErrors := namespaceRefusalErrors(mirrorTargets, updreq.Commands)

663		commandsWithoutNamespaceGate := filterSurvivingCommands(updreq.Commands, otherEarlyPreCASErrors)
664		earlyPreCASErrors := joinErrors(otherEarlyPreCASErrors, namespaceErrors)
665		commandsAfterEarlyRejects := filterSurvivingCommands(updreq.Commands, earlyPreCASErrors)

667		// Determine if any command that can still commit needs the packfile. Commands
668		// already rejected by policy should not force us to ingest otherwise
669		// unreachable objects.
670		needPackfile := commandsNeedPack(commandsAfterEarlyRejects)

# Repository guidance

This is the canonical, vendor-neutral guidance for coding agents and contributors
working in this repository. `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this file so every agent
runtime reads the same rules. Tool-specific integrations under `.claude/`,
`.codex/`, `.opencode/`, and `.pi/` provide hooks or skills; they do not override
this file, user instructions, or repository invariants.

## Working in this repository

- Inspect `git status` before editing. Preserve unrelated changes and untracked
  files; never discard work you did not create.
- Keep one writer per worktree. Parallel agents are useful for read-only
  exploration and review; use separate worktrees for parallel implementation.
  The primary agent owns decisions, integration, and final verification.
- Read the relevant implementation, tests, docs, and ADRs before changing a
  subsystem. Source and tests win when a living document has drifted; ADRs record
  historical decisions and may describe an earlier production state.
- Prefer small, reviewable changes. Do not silently widen the task into adjacent
  cleanup, but call out stale or risky adjacent behavior.
- Do not start Docker containers. Ask the user to start local dependencies when
  required.

## Applications and ownership

This monorepo contains multiple independently deployed production applications.
A shared Go module does not imply a shared runtime or rollout.

| Application | Purpose | Primary code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entiredb** | Git data plane: smart HTTP, refs, object storage, replication, repair, and repo APIs | `cmd/entiredb`, `internal/entireserver`, `server/`, `refstore/`, `objstore/`, `diss/`, `dht/`, `packfile/` |

ADRs live in `docs/adrs/` and use `YYYYMMDD-short-description.md`. Read relevant
ADRs before changing a system they cover.

Write an ADR only for a decision that is expensive to reverse. Examples are a
persisted data format, a protocol between applications, a new datastore or
external service, and a consistency or topology model. Do not write an ADR for
a feature, an endpoint, a package, a field, a gate, or a refactor. The code,
tests, and PR description record those.

the decision, and the rejected alternatives. Do not name functions, fields,
files, flags, or per-request checks. Those details change in the next PR, and
the ADR then misleads.

Do not edit an old ADR to match the code. Do not write a new ADR because an old
one's detail drifted. Supersede an ADR only when its decision reverses.

## GitHub and pull requests

The `origin` remote uses the `entire://` proxy scheme rather than a github.com
URL, so `gh` cannot infer the GitHub repository. Always pass the repo explicitly,
and usually the head branch:

```bash
gh pr create --repo entirehq/entiredb --head <branch-name>
gh pr list --repo entirehq/entiredb --head <branch-name>
```

Match recent merged PR style:

- Preserve an existing `entire-trail-link` comment block.
- Use a concise scoped title when appropriate, e.g. `repoapi: fix detached
  reader lifetime`, `core/regional: add email lookup storage`, or `dev: mark
  bootstrap tasks interactive`.
- Use sentence style after the scope; do not force conventional-commit prefixes.
- Prefer `## Why`, `## What`, and `## Verification`/`## Tests`. Explain behavior
  and rollout risk, not just files changed.
- Put follow-ups and deferred work in their own section.
- For production changes, include compatibility, rollout/rollback, observability,
  and tests where relevant.

## Engineering style

In priority order:

1. Preserve correctness, security, privacy, and customer data.
2. Make the change pass focused tests and production-safe rollout constraints.
3. Reveal intent with explicit control flow and precise names.
4. Remove duplication of knowledge.
5. Keep the design minimal; abstractions must earn their cost.

Write tests alongside behavior changes. Handle errors at the call site, keep hot
paths simple, and measure before optimizing. Refactor first when it makes the
behavioral change safer; do not mix broad cleanup into a risky production
change.

Be direct about uncertainty. Correct false assumptions, propose a better option
when one exists, and escalate product, architecture, privacy, or rollout choices
instead of guessing.

## Writing style

Prose in this repository follows the core rules of ASD-STE100 Simplified
Technical English. This covers code comments, Go doc comments, ADRs, runbooks,
and PR bodies. The approved-word dictionary is not required; the sentence rules
are.

- Put one topic in each sentence. Put one instruction in each sentence.
- Keep descriptive sentences to 25 words or fewer and procedural sentences to
  20 words or fewer.
- Use the active voice and the present tense. Name the subject.
- Use one term for one concept in a document. Do not vary terms for style.
- Do not use noun clusters longer than three words.
- Write instructions as commands, not as "-ing" forms or passive requests.

Write a comment only when it captures non-obvious intent, an invariant, an
external contract, a concurrency or ordering hazard, a security or
data-residency rule, a migration constraint, concise documentation required for
an exported Go API, a tool directive, or the reason a regression test exists.
Do not narrate control flow or restate names, types, or assertions. The slop
monitor in `.entire/runners/trail-slop.json` grades comments by this same list;
change both together.

Go doc comments keep the Go convention: the first sentence starts with the
identifier name. That convention and these rules are compatible.

Before:

```go
// The lock is being acquired here so that concurrent modifications that might
// be happening from other callers are serialized, which prevents them from
// overwriting each other's changes based on stale reads of the row.
```

After:

```go
// FOR UPDATE locks the row before the new list is computed. A concurrent edit
// waits instead of merging from a stale read.
```

# Repository guidance

This is the canonical, vendor-neutral guidance for coding agents and contributors
working in this repository. `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this file so every agent
runtime reads the same rules. Tool-specific integrations under `.claude/`,
`.codex/`, `.opencode/`, and `.pi/` provide hooks or skills; they do not override
this file, user instructions, or repository invariants.

## Working in this repository

- Inspect `git status` before editing. Preserve unrelated changes and untracked
  files; never discard work you did not create.
- Keep one writer per worktree. Parallel agents are useful for read-only
  exploration and review; use separate worktrees for parallel implementation.
  The primary agent owns decisions, integration, and final verification.
- Read the relevant implementation, tests, docs, and ADRs before changing a
  subsystem. Source and tests win when a living document has drifted; ADRs record
  historical decisions and may describe an earlier production state.
- Prefer small, reviewable changes. Do not silently widen the task into adjacent
  cleanup, but call out stale or risky adjacent behavior.
- Do not start Docker containers. Ask the user to start local dependencies when
  required.

## Applications and ownership

This monorepo contains multiple independently deployed production applications.
A shared Go module does not imply a shared runtime or rollout.

| Application | Purpose | Primary code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entiredb** | Git data plane: smart HTTP, refs, object storage, replication, repair, and repo APIs | `cmd/entiredb`, `internal/entireserver`, `server/`, `refstore/`, `objstore/`, `diss/`, `dht/`, `packfile/` |
| **entire-core** | Control plane: identity, OAuth/OIDC, JWT/JWKS, SpiceDB authorization, resource lifecycle, regional PII, and console | `cmd/entire-core`, `internal/entirecore`, `core/`, `api/corev1/`, `frontend/` |
| **entire-ci-webhooks** | CI webhook/event bridge with its own deployment and datastore | `cmd/entire-ci-webhooks`, `internal/ciwebhooks/` |
| **entire-backup** | Backup and restore tooling, also shipped as a separately deployed job | `cmd/entire-backup`, backup-related client/server packages |

Other `cmd/` packages are CLIs, operator tools, test utilities, or support
services. See `docs/repo-map.md` for the current binary and package map.

### Naming

- Call the data-plane application and binary **entiredb** in new prose. The old
  name `entire-server` remains in some package names, telemetry identifiers,
  workflow filenames, fleet resources, and historical documents; do not use it
  as the current application name.
- `entire-core` is not a subsystem inside entiredb. Treat its APIs, data,
  migrations, deployment modes, and release risk as a separate application.
- Call the CI bridge **entire-ci-webhooks**, or **ci-webhooks** after the first
  use.  It is standalone from `entire-core`.
- The user-facing control-plane CLI (`entire`) and `git-remote-entire` live in
  [github.com/entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli). `entire-repo` in
  this repo contains data-plane git-content commands only.

### Application-specific context

Read the root guide first, then load the relevant application guide **before
editing** that application:

| Scope | Typical paths | Required guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entiredb** | `cmd/entiredb`, `internal/entireserver`, `server`, `refstore`, `objstore`, `diss`, `dht`, `packfile`, `api/repov1` | `docs/agent-guides/entiredb.md` |
| **entire-core** | `cmd/entire-core`, `internal/entirecore`, `core`, `api/corev1`, `frontend` | `docs/agent-guides/entire-core.md` |

Route by behavior and contract, not only by file location. For shared packages,
generated contracts, or ambiguous ownership, inspect callers and deployment
workflows and read every affected application guide. Cross-application changes
require both guides. Applications without a dedicated guide use this root guide
plus their nearest README and living documentation.

### Cross-application changes

When a change crosses an application boundary:

- identify the producer, consumer, and owner of every API, message, table, and
  generated client involved;
- assume deployments can be on different versions during rollout and rollback;
- document rollout order and failure behavior;
- test both sides of the contract; and
- inspect the corresponding path filters and deployment workflows in
  `.github/workflows/`.

For deployed topology, cluster/region ownership, and Flux overlays, inspect the
sibling `../fleet` repository. This repo does not define the complete production
topology.

## Production and compatibility

This system is in production and stores customer data. Compatibility and safe
rollout are the default.

- Preserve public API, CLI, persisted-data, Git-format, event/message, and
  cross-service compatibility unless an explicitly approved migration says
  otherwise.
- Design for mixed versions. entiredb rolls node by node; entire-core runs across
  global/regional deployments; CLIs and external consumers may lag the server.
- Prefer expand/migrate/contract: add a compatible shape, deploy readers and
  writers, migrate or backfill separately, observe it, then remove the old
  shape in a later deployment.
- Treat database migrations as forward-only in operation. A `Down` section is
  not a rollback plan. Rollback normally means old code running against the
  newer schema.
- Do not drop or reinterpret stored data, claims, fields, refs, events, or
  permissions without a recovery plan and evidence that old consumers and data
  are gone.
- Breaking changes require an explicit rollout, rollback, observability, and
  consumer-coordination plan. Include companion changes in `fleet`,
  `entireio/cli`, or other repositories when applicable.
- Feature flags, shadow modes, dual writes, and compatibility adapters are valid
  rollout tools when they reduce production risk. Give each a safe default,
  owner, removal condition, and cleanup plan; do not leave two permanent paths.
- Security, authorization, and privacy/data-residency boundaries must fail
  closed; never weaken them merely to preserve availability. Durability and
  deletion workflows must preserve data or retry safely rather than reporting
  success before their guarantees are met.

Historical ADRs and specs that say the code was not in production describe the
state when they were written; they do not override this policy.

## Commands and local validation

```bash
# Focused test. Prefer the task over bare `go test`: it exports env setup.
mise run test ./path/to/package --run TestName
mise run test ./path/to/package --run TestName --count 20   # flake hunt

# Repository test task (requires the local Postgres sidecar; DB-backed core
# packages also require CockroachDB and SpiceDB from dev:prereqs)
mise run test
mise run test --race
mise run test --shard db       # CockroachDB/SpiceDB packages
mise run test --shard postgres # remaining packages

# Full lint before committing
mise run lint
mise run lint --fix            # opt-in; review every generated fix

# Generate protobuf outputs after changing their inputs
mise run protobuf
```

Database-backed tests do not start dependencies. In linked worktrees, ask the
developer to run `mise run dev:prereqs`; agents must not start containers.

Use `mise run test`, not bare `go test`, for DB-backed packages. It supplies
the worktree namespace and private service endpoints. A linked worktree has a
private Compose project for Postgres, NATS, CockroachDB, and SpiceDB. Compose
assigns dynamic host ports and project-scoped named volumes. Services and
mutable data remain private. Immutable migration backups are shared by content
hash and the pinned CockroachDB image version through the shared host cache.
The worktree reuses the primary checkout certificate bundle through `certs/`.

A linked `mise run dev:reset` removes only its Compose project and named
volumes. The primary checkout retains the full reset of its shared containers.
Host application listeners remain shared and use fixed ports. Run one full
local application stack at a time. DB and full runs use `-p=4`; `--shard postgres`
needs Postgres but not CockroachDB, NATS, or SpiceDB.

### Local test selection

- Run focused tests for each changed package first.
- Require a backend only when a test verifies its real backend contract.
- Do not run a full DB shard beside another worktree DB suite.
- After one DB test fails because test infrastructure is unavailable, such as a
  CockroachDB startup timeout, stop local retries. Do not defer a test assertion
  or application error to CI. Use exact-head CI for the affected suite.
- `ENTIRE_TEST_DB_PARALLELISM=1` limits package fan-out only.

`mise run lint` runs Go lint, gofmt, gofix, module tidiness, migration checks,
protobuf checks, shellcheck, actionlint, and repository-specific join guards.
Auto-fix is deliberately opt-in because static-analysis quick fixes can change
behavior.

Validation expectations:

- Run targeted unit tests for every package changed.
- Run integration tests you add or modify. Let CI run unrelated integration
  suites.
- For cross-application changes, validate each affected application and the
  shared contract, not only the package where the edit landed.
- For docs-only changes, run the cheapest relevant structural checks and
  `git diff --check`; the full lint remains the pre-commit standard.
- Report commands not run and why. A skipped dependency-backed test is not a
  pass.

Write every new test parallel. Apply the rule everywhere. `paralleltest`
enforces it in the packages allowlisted in `.golangci.yaml`, and an exception
there needs `//nolint:paralleltest // <reason>`.

A parallel test must own the rows it asserts on. Scope each query by an ID the
test creates, and take the package's shared pool. A test that counts or lists
across the whole database cannot do that, so give it `testutil.ClonedPool` and
its own database. A global assertion against a shared pool passes only while no
neighbour writes a matching row.

## Contracts and configuration

- Treat public APIs, CLIs, protobufs, OpenAPI types, JWT claims, audience/scope
  values, persisted records, and event envelopes as compatibility surfaces.
- Internal transports vary by boundary; do not guess—inspect the caller,
  listener, generated contract, and relevant application guide.
- Prefer `ENTIRE_` for new application-specific environment variables. Reuse an
  established ecosystem variable or existing bare deployment contract only
  when that is intentional and documented.
- Never add a configuration knob for behavior that should be an invariant.
- **GitHub installation-token `reason` strings are a cross-repo contract with
  entire-api, enforced nowhere.** entire-api passes a `reason` to
  `POST /sts/github-installation-token`; Core admits an exact `(workload, reason)`
  pair. The two lists are independent string literals in two repositories, so a
  reason entire-api adds is simply denied in production until a row is added
  here. Admitting one takes **two edits in `core/api/sts_token.go`**, and one
  without the other still fails:
  1. a row in `githubInstallationTokenCapabilities` (admits the key), and
  2. the reason added to that authority's arm of `validFor` (grants the
     authority). A row without a `validFor` entry is rejected.

  Because every caller on the entire-api side is best-effort by design — a
  non-OK `Result` is logged and swallowed — a missing reason surfaces as the
  *feature quietly not working*, never as an error. Two have shipped dead this
  way (`runner_checks_failed`, fixed in #3218; `trail_gate_checks_resync`, in
  ENT-1702), and one of them was worse than a no-op: entire-api's gate
  recomputer treats a failed check-run read as fail-closed, so the denied mint
  flipped the checks gate to a blocking `error`. When you add or rename a
  reason on either side, grep the other repository for it in the same change.

Each CLI exposing a `docs` subcommand can print its complete generated command
reference:

```bash
entire-repo docs
entiredbctl docs
entire-core docs
entire-backup docs
```

Use this instead of guessing flags from stale prose.

## Tests and debugging

- Unit tests live beside source; integration tests live under `test/`.
- Common helpers live under `test/testutils/`, `test/testserver/`,
  `test/testgit/`, and `test/workloads/`.
- `mise run test` excludes the `entire.io/test` integration subtree and handles
  nested modules under `modules/` separately.
- Do not jump from a race report to “add a mutex.” Reproduce the ownership bug,
  choose the smallest synchronization or ownership fix, and run the affected
  test with `-race`.

## Code navigation and documentation

For Go symbols, prefer `gopls` and `go doc` when available:

```bash
go doc <pkg>.<Symbol>
gopls references <file>:<line>:<col>
gopls implementation <file>:<line>:<col>
gopls call_hierarchy <file>:<line>:<col>
```

Use text search for strings, comments, configuration, and when the symbol is not
yet known.

Start with:

- `docs/agent-guides/` — conditional application-specific instructions
- `docs/repo-map.md` — binaries, package ownership, ports, topology
- `docs/architecture.md` — entiredb data-plane design
- `core/README.md` — entire-core application and package map
- `docs/auth.md` — canonical identity/authentication/authorization model
- `docs/glossary.md` — domain terminology
- `docs/runbooks/` and `docs/postmortems/` — production operations and failure
  history
- `../fleet` — actual deployment manifests and overlays

ADRs live in `docs/adrs/` and use `YYYYMMDD-short-description.md`. Read relevant
ADRs before changing a system they cover.

Write an ADR only for a decision that is expensive to reverse. Examples are a
persisted data format, a protocol between applications, a new datastore or
external service, and a consistency or topology model. Do not write an ADR for
a feature, an endpoint, a package, a field, a gate, or a refactor. The code,
tests, and PR description record those.

Keep an ADR at the level of the decision. State the problem, the constraints,
the decision, and the rejected alternatives. Do not name functions, fields,
files, flags, or per-request checks. Those details change in the next PR, and
the ADR then misleads.

Do not edit an old ADR to match the code. Do not write a new ADR because an old
one's detail drifted. Supersede an ADR only when its decision reverses.

## GitHub and pull requests

The `origin` remote uses the `entire://` proxy scheme rather than a github.com
URL, so `gh` cannot infer the GitHub repository. Always pass the repo explicitly,
and usually the head branch:

```bash
gh pr create --repo entirehq/entiredb --head <branch-name>
gh pr list --repo entirehq/entiredb --head <branch-name>
```

Match recent merged PR style:

- Preserve an existing `entire-trail-link` comment block.
- Use a concise scoped title when appropriate, e.g. `repoapi: fix detached
  reader lifetime`, `core/regional: add email lookup storage`, or `dev: mark
  bootstrap tasks interactive`.
- Use sentence style after the scope; do not force conventional-commit prefixes.
- Prefer `## Why`, `## What`, and `## Verification`/`## Tests`. Explain behavior
  and rollout risk, not just files changed.
- Put follow-ups and deferred work in their own section.
- For production changes, include compatibility, rollout/rollback, observability,
  and tests where relevant.

## Engineering style

In priority order:

1. Preserve correctness, security, privacy, and customer data.
2. Make the change pass focused tests and production-safe rollout constraints.
3. Reveal intent with explicit control flow and precise names.
4. Remove duplication of knowledge.
5. Keep the design minimal; abstractions must earn their cost.

Write tests alongside behavior changes. Handle errors at the call site, keep hot
paths simple, and measure before optimizing. Refactor first when it makes the
behavioral change safer; do not mix broad cleanup into a risky production
change.

Be direct about uncertainty. Correct false assumptions, propose a better option
when one exists, and escalate product, architecture, privacy, or rollout choices
instead of guessing.

## Writing style

Prose in this repository follows the core rules of ASD-STE100 Simplified
Technical English. This covers code comments, Go doc comments, ADRs, runbooks,
and PR bodies. The approved-word dictionary is not required; the sentence rules
are.

- Put one topic in each sentence. Put one instruction in each sentence.
- Keep descriptive sentences to 25 words or fewer and procedural sentences to
  20 words or fewer.
- Use the active voice and the present tense. Name the subject.
- Use one term for one concept in a document. Do not vary terms for style.
- Do not use noun clusters longer than three words.
- Write instructions as commands, not as "-ing" forms or passive requests.

Write a comment only when it captures non-obvious intent, an invariant, an
external contract, a concurrency or ordering hazard, a security or
data-residency rule, a migration constraint, concise documentation required for
an exported Go API, a tool directive, or the reason a regression test exists.
Do not narrate control flow or restate names, types, or assertions. The slop
monitor in `.entire/runners/trail-slop.json` grades comments by this same list;
change both together.

Go doc comments keep the Go convention: the first sentence starts with the
identifier name. That convention and these rules are compatible.

Before:

```go
// The lock is being acquired here so that concurrent modifications that might
// be happening from other callers are serialized, which prevents them from
// overwriting each other's changes based on stale reads of the row.
```

After:

```go
// FOR UPDATE locks the row before the new list is computed. A concurrent edit
// waits instead of merging from a stale read.
```

1	// Package refpolicy is the single source of truth for how entiredb treats the
2	// reserved and internal Git ref namespaces. It answers three questions that
3	// were previously decided in three places and drifted:
4	//
5	//   - Push: may this caller push this ref, or is the namespace reserved?
6	//     (was server/githttp/receive_pack.go's reservedPush* slices)
7	//   - Fetch: is this ref hidden from advertisement for this caller?
8	//     (uploadpack.hideRefs, previously wired nil everywhere)
9	//   - Recording: should a push to this ref produce a signed RSL entry?
10	//     (was rslstore.ShouldRecord's denylist)
11	//
12	// Recording starts from fetch visibility: a hidden ref is never signed. Two
13	// visible namespaces are carved out as well. Unmirrored branches
14	// (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/*) stay visible on fetch but are never mirrored
15	// to GitHub, and git-sync's transfer scaffolding (refs/gitsync/**) stays visible
16	// so a bootstrap can resume but exists only on a replication target (see
17	// ShouldRecord). The coverage mode then narrows what remains to branches, tags,
18	// and checkpoints (see CoveredByMode). Deriving visibility and the recording
19	// base from one hidden set keeps a hidden ref from ever being signed.
20	//
21	// The policy is layered as a chain of command (see resolve): a base layer of
22	// fleet-wide invariants, then per-domain deltas (native vs GitHub-mirror repos),
23	// then per-caller carve-outs. Each layer may only ADD restrictions; the only
24	// ways to loosen are an explicit workload carve-out (push) or the trusted-reader
25	// exemption (fetch). Deny-by-default, fail-closed.
26	package refpolicy
27	
28	import (
29		"slices"
30		"strings"
31	
32		"entire.io/core/servicetoken"
33		"entire.io/internal/go-git/plumbing/transport/hiderefs"
34		"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/rsl"
35	)
36	
37	// Canonical ref namespaces. These names previously lived as unexported
38	// constants in receive_pack.go, rslstore/writer.go, and refstore; this package
39	// is now their one home.
40	const (
41		// GittufPrefix is gittuf's reserved namespace (RSL, policy, policy-staging,
42		// attestations). entiredb owns it server-side; direct client pushes to any
43		// refs/gittuf/* are refused.
44		GittufPrefix = "refs/gittuf/"
45		// RSLRef is the gittuf Reference State Log, written server-side by rslstore.
46		// Bound to gittuf's own constant so the recording carve-out (ShouldRecord)
47		// cannot drift from the ref gittuf actually writes and start signing the RSL
48		// into itself.
49		RSLRef = rsl.Ref
50		// PolicyStagingRef is gittuf's staging policy ref. gittuf keeps its own copy
51		// unexported (unlike rsl.Ref), so this literal must be kept equal to it by
52		// hand.
53		PolicyStagingRef = "refs/gittuf/policy-staging"
54		// PolicyRef is the repo's root of trust. It is client-visible so clients can
55		// verify against it, so it is neither hidden nor exempt from recording.
56		PolicyRef = "refs/gittuf/policy"
57	
58		// ManagedMetaPrefix is the git-meta service's shared metadata namespace,
59		// reserved for direct client pushes but writable by the entire-api workload.
60		// It is client-visible and recorded.
61		ManagedMetaPrefix = "refs/meta/entire/"
62	
63		// InternalPrefix, LocalPrefix, and EntirePrefix are entiredb-internal
64		// namespaces: reserved from direct client push, hidden from external fetch,
65		// and not recorded. Two sub-namespaces below are exceptions on all three
66		// counts, because a client owns each: EntireCheckpointsPrefix and
67		// EntirePoliciesPrefix. refs/local/* holds node-local refs that never leave
68		// the server, so they are never advertised and users cannot push them.
69		InternalPrefix = "refs/internal"
70		LocalPrefix    = "refs/local"
71		EntirePrefix   = "refs/entire"
72	
73		// HeadsPrefix and TagsPrefix are the two ordinary user-facing namespaces.
74		// They carry no policy of their own here. They exist so the coverage modes
75		// in coverage.go name them from the same place as every other namespace
76		// literal rather than re-spelling them.
77		HeadsPrefix = "refs/heads/"
78		TagsPrefix  = "refs/tags/"
79	
80		// GitSyncScaffoldPrefix is git-sync's own temp-ref namespace on a
81		// replication TARGET: a batched bootstrap parks each branch at
82		// refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch> and removes it when the branch
83		// lands. It is transfer scaffolding the sync writes and deletes itself, not
84		// repository content, and it exists ONLY on the target — the primary never
85		// holds one, so the primary's RSL never attests one.
86		//
87		// It is carved out of recording for that reason, and deliberately NOT hidden:
88		// git-sync reads its own scaffolding back from the target's advertisement to
89		// resume an interrupted bootstrap, so hiding it would break the resume.
90		// See server/githttp's gitsyncScaffoldPrefix, which pins the same literal for
91		// the writer-scope gate.
92		GitSyncScaffoldPrefix = "refs/gitsync/"
93	
94		// EntireCheckpointsPrefix is the checkpoint sub-namespace of refs/entire. It
95		// is the exception to the refs/entire rules: checkpoints are client-visible
96		// (un-hidden), user-amendable (pushable), and therefore recorded, while the
97		// rest of refs/entire stays hidden and reserved. refs/entire/checkpoints/* is
98		// written both by the entire-api path (repoapi commit_create) and by users.
99		EntireCheckpointsPrefix = "refs/entire/checkpoints"
100	
101		// EntirePoliciesPrefix is the checkpoint-policy sub-namespace of
102		// refs/entire. The entire CLI owns it: checkpointpolicy.Push writes
103		// refs/entire/policies/checkpoint, and the same package lists and fetches
104		// that ref to compare a local policy against the remote baseline.
105		//
106		// It therefore follows the EntireCheckpointsPrefix rules. The CLI is an
107		// ordinary client, so the ref is pushable by every caller, and it is
108		// advertised: a hidden ref returns nothing to the CLI's ls-remote and
109		// fails its fetch. It is not a branch, tag, or checkpoint, so no coverage
110		// mode signs it.
111		//
112		// Reserving this namespace refused two writers at once (ENT-2479): the
113		// CLI's own push, and the mirror worker's GitHub sync, which replays the
114		// ref a CLI left on the upstream. A worker-only carve-out fixes the sync
115		// and leaves every CLI user refused, so the opening is not scoped to a
116		// workload.
117		//
118		// entiredb stores the content and interprets none of it. Nothing here
119		// reads policy.json. Giving this ref a meaning in entiredb is a separate
120		// change: the refs already in the fleet were written under no server-side
121		// rule, so that change needs a migration over them, validation at the
122		// write path, or both, before anything may trust their content.
123		EntirePoliciesPrefix = "refs/entire/policies"
124	
125		// entireHeadsAnchor, unmirroredAnchor and nativeAnchor are the directory
126		// anchors that protect the two mirror-only Entire-owned branch namespaces
127		// (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/* and refs/heads/entire/native/*). They are
128		// reserved on GitHub-mirror repos only; a native repo may use them as
129		// ordinary branches.
130		entireHeadsAnchor = "refs/heads/entire"
131		unmirroredAnchor  = "refs/heads/entire/unmirrored"
132		nativeAnchor      = "refs/heads/entire/native"
133	)
134	
135	// Domain is the class of repository a ref policy applies to. Native repos and
136	// GitHub mirrors share a base policy and differ only in their deltas.
137	type Domain int
138	
139	const (
140		// DomainNative is an Entire-native repository.
141		DomainNative Domain = iota
142		// DomainGitHubMirror is a repository mirrored from GitHub.
143		DomainGitHubMirror
144	)
145	
146	// DomainForMirror maps the repo row's is_mirror flag onto a Domain, keeping the
147	// classification in one place without coupling this package to repostore.
148	func DomainForMirror(isMirror bool) Domain {
149		if isMirror {
150			return DomainGitHubMirror
151		}
152		return DomainNative
153	}
154	
155	// Caller is the request identity a policy needs. Workload is the mTLS workload
156	// identity (empty for a public client). TrustedReader marks a caller that must
157	// see every ref regardless of hideRefs, i.e. backup/restore capture, so a
158	// bundle stays complete. The server adapts its request principal onto this.
159	type Caller struct {
160		Workload      servicetoken.Workload
161		TrustedReader bool
162		// NativeReplication marks the mirror-worker push that replicates a native
163		// primary's refs into a native-mirror PLACEMENT. It is the one caller that
164		// may write gittuf's namespace (see the carve-out in baseRules), because
165		// that push republishes trust material the primary already signed rather
166		// than authoring any. The server sets it from the repos row and the request
167		// principal together, never from the request alone.
168		NativeReplication bool
169	}
170	
171	// PushCheck is the reserved-ref verdict for one ref and caller.
172	type PushCheck struct {
173		// Reserved reports whether the ref falls in a reserved namespace.
174		Reserved bool
175		// Bucket is the matched rule, a low-cardinality metric label; "" when not
176		// reserved.
177		Bucket string
178		// Allowed reports whether this caller may push the ref: true when the ref is
179		// not reserved, or a carve-out lifts the reservation for this caller.
180		Allowed bool
181	}
182	
183	// carveOut lifts the reserved-ref gate on a namespace for named workloads.
184	// nativeReplicationOnly narrows it further, to the native-mirror replication
185	// push alone: the workload identity says WHO is calling, and that flag says
186	// WHICH of its pushes qualifies. A carve-out needs both when the same workload
187	// also runs pushes that must stay blocked.
188	type carveOut struct {
189		prefix                string
190		writers               []servicetoken.Workload
191		nativeReplicationOnly bool
192	}
193	
194	// rules is one layer's contribution to a policy. Layers are merged (see
195	// resolve); every field is additive.
196	type rules struct {
197		reservedPrefixes []string // matched with a trailing slash (path prefix)
198		reservedExact    []string // matched whole
199		pushOpenPrefixes []string // sub-prefixes pushable for ALL callers despite a reserved parent
200		carveOuts        []carveOut
201		hidePatterns     []string // uploadpack.hideRefs syntax (hiderefs.IsHidden)
202	}
203	
204	// Policy is the resolved, immutable ref policy for one domain. Its zero value is
205	// not valid; obtain one from a Resolver.
206	type Policy struct {
207		r rules
208	}
209	
210	// baseRules are the fleet-wide invariants that apply to every repo, whatever its
211	// domain. Each entry below notes why it is reserved/hidden and whether it can be
212	// overridden. The two override mechanisms are distinct:
213	//
214	//   - Push reservations are lifted two ways: a workload carve-out (see
215	//     carveOuts) opens a namespace to a named workload, and a pushOpenPrefixes
216	//     entry opens a sub-namespace to every caller (e.g. refs/entire/checkpoints/*
217	//     inside reserved refs/entire). The domain layer can add but never remove a
218	//     base reservation (tighten-only).
219	//   - Hide patterns are overridable per-subtree by a "!"-prefixed exception,
220	//     since hiderefs matching is last-match-wins (see hidePatterns).
221	func baseRules() rules {
222		return rules{
223			// Reserved from client push, matched as a path prefix (trailing slash
224			// required). Overridable only by a workload carve-out where noted.
225			reservedPrefixes: []string{
226				// Git convention for server-internal refs; also hidden from fetch
227				// (hidePatterns). Blocking push closes the write side. No carve-out.
228				InternalPrefix + "/",
229				// Node-local refs that never leave the server; also hidden from fetch
230				// (hidePatterns) and excluded from recording. Blocking push closes the
231				// write side. No carve-out.
232				LocalPrefix + "/",
233				// entiredb-managed refs; also hidden from fetch and excluded from
234				// recording. Reserved from direct client push, EXCEPT the two
235				// sub-namespaces in pushOpenPrefixes below: checkpoints and
236				// policies, both of which the entire CLI writes. The remainder is
237				// written only through server-side paths (not receive-pack), so
238				// this gate does not block them. No carve-out.
239				EntirePrefix + "/",
240				// Git object-replacement: a ref here rewrites how every cloner sees an
241				// object, so push is object substitution against all clients. No carve-out.
242				"refs/replace/",
243				// git bisect's session-local refs; meaningless on the server. No carve-out.
244				"refs/bisect/",
245				// The client's own remote-tracking view; no server-side meaning. No carve-out.
246				"refs/remotes/",
247				// Entire's structured-metadata namespace (ENT-1106), reserved so writes
248				// funnel through the git-meta service, which owns format + authz.
249				// OVERRIDABLE: the entire-api carve-out below lifts it for nested refs.
250				ManagedMetaPrefix,
251				// Git's GIT_NAMESPACE feature; entiredb uses one repo per ULID and never
252				// namespaces, so a push here makes double-nested refs no tool expects.
253				// No carve-out.
254				"refs/namespaces/",
255				// Prefix-form custom stash layouts (the bare refs/stash is an anchor
256				// below). No carve-out.
257				"refs/stash/",
258				// gittuf's namespace: the RSL is server-managed and user-authored
259				// policy/RSL is not supported yet, so the whole namespace is closed to
260				// direct client push. refs/gittuf/policy stays fetch-visible for
261				// verification. The server's own RSL writes bypass this gate.
262				// OVERRIDABLE: the native-replication carve-out below lifts it for the
263				// mirror worker replicating a primary into a native mirror.
264				GittufPrefix,
265			},
266			// Directory anchors: the bare namespace roots, reserved exact so a leaf ref
267			// squatting one cannot D/F-conflict with (and thereby block) every ref
268			// beneath it. Reserved for EVERY caller, carve-out workloads included: a
269			// carve-out matches by prefix + "/", so it never reaches the bare anchor,
270			// and the anchor's only legitimate writers create nested refs. Not
271			// overridable. refs/heads and refs/tags matter most on an uninitialised
272			// repo, where nothing beneath them exists yet to reject the squat; ordinary
273			// refs/heads/* and refs/tags/* stay pushable.
274			reservedExact: []string{
275				"refs/heads", // blocks squatting the branch root
276				"refs/tags",  // blocks squatting the tag root
277				"refs/stash",
278				"refs/meta",
279				"refs/meta/entire",
280				"refs/gittuf",
281				EntirePrefix,            // refs/entire anchor, matching its reserved prefix above
282				EntireCheckpointsPrefix, // refs/entire/checkpoints anchor, so squatting the bare leaf can't block the pushable checkpoints/* subtree
283				EntirePoliciesPrefix,    // refs/entire/policies anchor, for the same reason as checkpoints above
284			},
285			// Pushable for ALL callers despite the reserved refs/entire/ parent: the
286			// entire CLI writes both sub-namespaces as an ordinary client, so a
287			// workload carve-out cannot express either one. Nested refs only; both
288			// bare anchors stay reserved (above). Both are un-hidden below, so
289			// recording follows the push opening rather than trailing it.
290			pushOpenPrefixes: []string{
291				EntireCheckpointsPrefix + "/",
292				EntirePoliciesPrefix + "/",
293			},
294			// Carve-outs are the ONLY way to lift a push reservation: each names the
295			// workload(s) allowed to write an otherwise-reserved namespace, matched by
296			// prefix + "/" (so the bare directory anchor stays reserved even for them).
297			carveOuts: []carveOut{
298				// entire-api owns refs/meta/entire/* (nested refs only).
299				{prefix: ManagedMetaPrefix, writers: []servicetoken.Workload{servicetoken.WorkloadEntireAPI}},
300				// The mirror worker replicates a native primary's refs/gittuf/** into a
301				// native-mirror placement (ENT-2423). Without this the bootstrap push
302				// carries the primary's policy and RSL, the whole push is refused, and
303				// the mirror can never hold managed refs — which is the very condition
304				// that selects bootstrap, so it never converges.
305				//
306				// The carve-out admits the push; it does not trust it. The mirror is a
307				// read-only copy, so what lands must be exactly what the primary
308				// published: refstore's fast-forward guard refuses a rewind of the
309				// namespace, the rooted-policy pin refuses a forward swap to a different
310				// root, and recording is suppressed under this mode so the placement
311				// never signs an entry of its own.
312				//
313				// The worker's GitHub-mirror syncs carry the same workload identity and
314				// are NOT covered: nativeReplicationOnly keys on the target being a
315				// native-mirror placement, so a GitHub mirror's trust material stays
316				// closed until ENT-1395 decides what it should be.
317				{
318					prefix:                GittufPrefix,
319					writers:               []servicetoken.Workload{servicetoken.WorkloadMirrorWorker},

321				},
322			},
323			// Hidden from external fetch: the entiredb-internal namespaces only. The
324			// RSL and policy-staging are deliberately NOT hidden (gittuf clients fetch
325			// the RSL to verify); they are carved out of recording instead, see
326			// ShouldRecord.
327			//
328			// OVERRIDABLE per subtree: hiderefs matching is last-match-wins, so a
329			// "!"-prefixed pattern appended AFTER a hide un-hides that subtree. The two
330			// exceptions below are exactly that: refs/entire is hidden, then each
331			// "!" pattern advertises one sub-namespace as a visible island inside the
332			// otherwise-hidden refs/entire. Of the two, only checkpoints are inside
333			// a coverage mode, so only checkpoint updates are signed.

336			// is an ordinary client, so hiding a ref does not merely conceal it: the
337			// CLI's ls-remote returns nothing and its fetch fails.
338			hidePatterns: []string{
339				InternalPrefix,                // server-internal refs (synthetic haves, etc.)
340				LocalPrefix,                   // node-local refs that never leave the server
341				EntirePrefix,                  // entiredb-managed refs (future trust material, etc.)
342				"!" + EntireCheckpointsPrefix, // un-hide checkpoints (must follow EntirePrefix)
343				"!" + EntirePoliciesPrefix,    // un-hide checkpoint policy (must follow EntirePrefix)
344			},

349	// tighten-only: it adds reservations/hides, never removes a base one. Only the
350	// GitHub-mirror domain adds rules today.

240		// channel rather than the public :443 listener — that listener
241		// explicitly rejects service-identity tokens (server/http.go:259-269,
242		// "split-listener policy"). The auth shape on this mount is the same
243		// Bearer→AuthenticateToken→AcceptGitAuth chain as :443, minus the
244		// service-subject reject — workload identity is already validated at
245		// the cert layer via WorkloadGate.
246		//
247		// githttp.Register attaches /git/repo/{id}/, /git/repo/{id}, and /git/
248		// to a sub-mux; the sub-mux is wrapped by WorkloadGate + inflight
249		// tracker before being mounted on the internal mux so cert-layer auth
250		// and shutdown coordination apply uniformly.
251		gitSvc := srv.NewGitHTTPService(cfg.HTTPInternalAdvertiseAddr)
252		gitMux := http.NewServeMux()
253		githttp.Register(gitMux, gitSvc, svcTokGitAuthMiddleware(cfg.Domain, srv.IssuerVerifier()), noopMiddleware)
254	
255		// Repo API (structured reads) on svctok. The entire-api ingester reads
256		// commit metadata through the huma /api/v1 surface here rather than
257		// cloning packs off the git mount above — same handler as the public
258		// :443 mount (server/http.go:401). Two auth shapes meet here, both
259		// behind WorkloadGate:
260		//   - entire-api is an internal workload authorized cert-only from this
261		//     server's inbound allowlist (docs/auth.md §3.2): its mTLS/SPIFFE
262		//     cert is the whole credential, granting a static repo-read class
263		//     with no Bearer and no SpiceDB lookup (svcTokRepoReadWorkloads).
264		//   - entire-mcp / entire-search / entire-api-gateway present a Bearer
265		//     JWT (per-user repo-scoped or account access), run through
266		//     the public Bearer/Basic→AuthenticateToken→AcceptRepoAPIAuth chain
267		//     minus the service-subject reject.
268		// withPeerLeaf stashes the peer leaf so AuthenticateToken can run the
269		// RFC 8705 §3 cnf check on the Bearer path; on this mTLS channel a
270		// repo-scoped token without cnf is rejected (the strict-cnf flip),
271		// while a cnf-less forwarded account access bearer is exempt and
272		// authorized live on sub. pool is non-nil here (guarded above), so
273		// NewRepoAPIService's ensureRepoStores populates the repourls store.
274		repoAPIHandler := repoapi.NewHandler(srv.NewRepoAPIService(cfg.HTTPInternalAdvertiseAddr), svcTokRepoAPIAuthMiddleware(cfg.Domain, srv.IssuerVerifier()), noopMiddleware)
275	
276		// http.Server.Shutdown returns when its deadline expires even if
277		// handlers are still running. Without this barrier, pgPool.Close (a
278		// later defer in serve.go) races those handlers and surfaces
279		// "closed pool" as gRPC Internal to the caller.
280		var inflight sync.WaitGroup
281		internalMux := http.NewServeMux()
282		// withPeerLeaf wraps the user-JWT mounts so server/auth's
283		// AuthenticateToken can run the RFC 8705 §3 cnf check. The
284		// RepoAdmin mount synthesises a servicetoken.Principal from the
285		// service:entiredb JWT issued at entire-core's /oauth/token; the
286		// wrapper's cnf branch reads the peer leaf off the same ctx.
287		repoAdminAuth := newRepoAdminAuth(srv.IssuerVerifier(), raHandler)
288		internalMux.Handle(raPath, withPeerLeaf(svcTokRepoAdminMount(cfg.Domain, repoAdminAuth, &inflight)))
289		// The worker-admitted procedures peel off the service-wide RepoAdmin
290		// mount above onto their own exact-path mounts (ServeMux prefers the
291		// longer pattern): the gate additionally admits the mirror-worker, and
292		// the auth wrapper accepts the same core bearer chain or the worker
293		// cert-only. Widening the shared mount instead would expose
294		// Provision/Delete to the worker.
295		sdbAuth := newSetDefaultBranchAuth(cfg.Domain, srv.IssuerVerifier(), raHandler)
296		for _, procedure := range svcTokWorkerAdmittedRepoAdminProcedures {
297			internalMux.Handle(procedure,
298				withPeerLeaf(svcTokSetDefaultBranchMount(cfg.Domain, sdbAuth, &inflight)))
299		}
300		// ListWritePositions (the resync sweep's delta read) peels onto its own
301		// exact-path mount too: the workload gate stays entire-core-only (same as
302		// the service-wide mount), but the auth wrapper additionally admits the
303		// cert-only entire-core shape — the sweep runs as a run-once CronJob with
304		// no serving core to mint cnf-bound bearers against, and the handler
305		// re-checks the workload off the stamped mTLS auth source.
306		lwpAuth := newListWritePositionsAuth(cfg.Domain, srv.IssuerVerifier(), raHandler)
307		internalMux.Handle(repoadminv1connect.RepoAdminListWritePositionsProcedure,
308			withPeerLeaf(svcTokRepoAdminMount(cfg.Domain, lwpAuth, &inflight)))
309		internalMux.Handle(adminPath, withPeerLeaf(svcTokAdminMount(cfg.Domain, adminHandler, &inflight)))
310		internalMux.Handle("/et/", withPeerLeaf(svcTokGitMount(cfg.Domain, gitMux, &inflight)))
311		internalMux.Handle("/git/", withPeerLeaf(svcTokGitMount(cfg.Domain, gitMux, &inflight)))
312		internalMux.Handle("/api/v1/", withPeerLeaf(svcTokRepoAPIMount(cfg.Domain, repoAPIHandler, &inflight)))
313	
314		// Stamp the serving node's identity on every response so callers reaching
315		// the data plane through this internal listener can tell which node
316		// handled the request (mirrors the public :443 mount). The internal
317		// advertise host is the readable name here.
318		stampNode := httputil.StampNodeMiddleware(srv.NodeID(), cfg.HTTPInternalAdvertiseAddr)
319	
320		// Strict handshake mTLS: RepoAdmin.Provision is called only by
321		// entire-core with a PCA-signed client cert. Bearer-only attempts
322		// fail the handshake before any middleware runs.
323		svcTokSrv := &http.Server{
324			Addr:              cfg.SvcTokListenAddr,
325			Handler:           stampNode(instrumentSvcTokHandler(internalMux)),
326			TLSConfig:         tlsConfig,
327			ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
328			// The fronting NLB does TCP-only health checks (see
329			// infra nlb-svctok.tf) which fail TLS at handshake; drop the
330			// resulting per-probe noise.
331			ErrorLog: slogutil.HTTPServerErrorLog(),
332		}
333		errCh := make(chan error, 1)
334		go func() {
335			// Empty cert+key paths fall back to svcTokSrv.TLSConfig in both cases.
336			var serveErr error
337			if svcTokLn != nil {
338				slogutil.Info(ctx, "service-token listener starting",
339					slog.String("addr", svcTokLn.Addr().String()),
340					slog.String("cert_source", files.source),
341					slog.Bool("socket_activated", true))
342				serveErr = svcTokSrv.ServeTLS(svcTokLn, "", "")
343			} else {
344				slogutil.Info(ctx, "service-token listener starting",
345					slog.String("addr", cfg.SvcTokListenAddr),
346					slog.String("cert_source", files.source),
347					slog.Bool("socket_activated", false))
348				serveErr = svcTokSrv.ListenAndServeTLS("", "")
349			}
350			if serveErr != nil && !errors.Is(serveErr, http.ErrServerClosed) {
351				slogutil.Error(ctx, "service-token listener exited", slog.Any("error", serveErr))
352				select {
353				case errCh <- fmt.Errorf("service-token listener: %w", serveErr):
354				case <-ctx.Done():
355				}
356			}
357		}()
358	
359		return errCh, func() {
360			// Graceful drain — bounded by the timeout. After this returns,
361			// in-flight handlers may still be running if the deadline expired.
362			shutdownHTTPServer(svcTokSrv, 5*time.Second, "service-token listener shutdown error")
363			// Force-close any connections Shutdown didn't drain so the handler
364			// goroutines observe ctx cancellation and unwind, then wait for
365			// them. Returning here without waiting would let pgPool.Close fire
366			// in serve.go while a handler is mid-pgx.Acquire, surfacing
367			// "closed pool" as Internal instead of a transient code.
368			_ = svcTokSrv.Close()
369			inflight.Wait()
370		}, nil
371	}
372	
373	// wireTrustPublisher populates the atomic trust-publication fields
374	// (PublishTrust, GetTrustReceipt) when this node has a signing RSL publish
375	// writer. A node without a signer (pw nil) leaves TrustPublisher nil and
376	// PublishTrust answers Unimplemented. Split out of the listener wiring so the
377	// "signer configured -> publisher wired" invariant is unit-testable without
378	// standing up the full service-token listener. pw is guarded before assignment
379	// so a nil concrete writer never becomes a non-nil (typed-nil) interface.
380	func wireTrustPublisher(svc *adminapi.RepoAdminService, pw *rslstore.RSLWriter, pool *pgxpool.Pool) {
381		if pw == nil {
382			return
383		}
384		svc.TrustPublisher = pw
385		svc.TrustRestorer = pw
386		svc.TrustReceipts = adminapi.NewPgTrustReceiptStore(pool)
387		svc.TrustPool = pool
388	}
389	
390	// svcTokAdminWorkloads is the allowlist of mTLS workloads admitted on the
391	// :8281 admin mount. entire-core remains the original caller for the
392	// console's cluster-inspection RPCs (per the comment above the mount).
393	// entire-backup joins for the three backup RPCs (ListAllRepos,
394	// DirtyReposSince, StreamRepoRefDigests) so the k8s CronJob path can reach them
395	// over internal DNS without going through the public ALB on :443 — this
396	// closes the gRPC-over-Cloudflare reachability hole that blocks the
397	// apex-DNS path until infra #387 lands.
398	//
399	// The in-handler `requireBackupAdminAccess` guard (server/adminapi/service.go)
400	// independently checks that the Bearer JWT is a TokenBackupAccess and
401	// rejects entire-core's TokenOpsAccess on the three backup RPCs; the gate
402	// here only narrows acceptance at the cert layer.
403	//
404	// entire-mcp joins to reach the read forensics RPCs from the hosted MCP
405	// surface. Admitting the workload here is a cert-layer narrowing only: the
406	// admin RPCs still require a cnf-bound ops-access JWT, so the leaf alone
407	// grants nothing.
408	var svcTokAdminWorkloads = []servicetoken.Workload{
409		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireCore,
410		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireBackup,
411		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireMCP,
412	}
413	
414	// svcTokGitWorkloads is the allowlist for the /et/ and /git/ mounts on
415	// :8281. Tighter than svcTokAdminWorkloads on purpose — see the
416	// comment above the internalMux.Handle("/et/", ...) call site.
417	//
418	// WorkloadEntireDB is admitted so on-node DISS callers (repair queue,
419	// catchup scanner, StoreRepoProvider-backfill) can fetch from peers on
420	// this mount instead of the public apex (ADR 20260518). Their outbound
421	// mTLS bundle carries a positive SPIFFE URI SAN (ENT-599) —
422	// callerFromMTLS resolves it to WorkloadEntireDB via the normal SPIFFE
423	// path, same as any other in-cluster workload. No Bearer is presented
424	// or required: internalWorkloadFromCert below synthesises an internal
425	// workload principal from the cert alone (the JWT-issuance path that
426	// used to gate this mount was retired).
427	//
428	// WorkloadMirrorWorker is the cluster-internal GitHub-mirror sync workload.
429	// Like entiredb peer-fetch it is authorized cert-only — no Bearer — but from
430	// the svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads allowlist below, which additionally grants
431	// push (to mirror-class repos).
432	//
433	// WorkloadPeregrine is authorized cert-only from svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads
434	// below (read-any-repo class).
435	//
436	// WorkloadEntireAPI is admitted for entire-api's git-meta receive-pack writes
437	// to refs/meta/entire/* (ENT-1106). WorkloadGate records its mTLS identity
438	// (servicetoken.CallerFromContext); receive-pack's namespaceWriters policy is
439	// what authorizes the write. See ADR 20260603-reserved-refs.md.
440	var svcTokGitWorkloads = []servicetoken.Workload{
441		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireBackup,
442		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireDB,
443		servicetoken.WorkloadMirrorWorker,
444		servicetoken.WorkloadPeregrine,
445		servicetoken.WorkloadEntireAPI,
446	}
447	
448	// svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads is this server's inbound allowlist for the static
449	// write-mirror permission class (docs/auth.md §3.2): internal workloads whose
450	// mTLS/SPIFFE certificate is the whole credential for pushing to mirror-class
451	// repos. A caller here needs no Bearer token and no SpiceDB grant — the
452	// allowlist entry is the authority. certOnlyGitPrincipal synthesises a
453	// reqctx.KindInternalWorkload principal with WriteMirror set (pull
454	// cluster-wide, push allowed; receive-pack rejects the push unless the target
455	// repo is mirror-class) for a no-Bearer request from one of these workloads.
456	//
457	// mirror-worker republishes what it just fetched from the GitHub upstream; as
458	// an internal workload it holds no svc_* row, mints no token, and needs no
459	// per-repo writer grant. Membership is a subset of svcTokGitWorkloads — a
460	// workload must clear the cert gate before it can be authorized cert-only.
461	var svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads = []servicetoken.Workload{
462		servicetoken.WorkloadMirrorWorker,
463	}
464	
465	// svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads is this server's inbound allowlist for the static
466	// read-any-repo permission class (docs/auth.md §3.2): the mTLS certificate
467	// alone authorizes cluster-wide pull, no Bearer and no SpiceDB grant.
468	// peregrine clones/fetches every repo for its search indexes and, as an
469	// internal workload, holds no svc_* row. Subset of svcTokGitWorkloads.
470	var svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads = []servicetoken.Workload{
471		servicetoken.WorkloadPeregrine,
472	}
473	
474	// svcTokRepoAPIWorkloads is the cert-layer allowlist (WorkloadGate) for the
475	// /api/v1/ huma repo-API mount on :8281 — which workloads may reach the mount
476	// at all. Tighter on purpose: adding a workload here exposes the structured
477	// repo-read surface to it, so it's a deliberate, reviewable one-liner. Pinned
478	// by TestSvcTokRepoAPIMountAllowedWorkloads. How each admitted workload then
479	// authorizes is decided in svcTokRepoAPIAuthMiddleware:
480	//
481	//   - entire-api and entire-search are authorized cert-only from
482	//     svcTokRepoReadWorkloads when they send no Bearer (docs/auth.md §3.2) —
483	//     no SpiceDB. The cert-only principal remains pull-only; CreateCommit has
484	//     a separate exact-workload capability gate in repoapi. entire-search
485	//     also forwards a per-user Bearer for its ordinary reads, which takes the
486	//     token path below.
487	//   - entire-mcp presents a Bearer JWT (per-user repo-scoped or account
488	//     access), so SpiceDB repo#pull is the real gate and the leaf alone
489	//     grants nothing.
490	//   - entire-api-gateway is entire-api's public reverse proxy. It always
491	//     forwards the caller's bearer, so it authorizes exactly like entire-mcp:
492	//     per-user, live against SpiceDB. It is a separate leaf from entire-api
493	//     so repoapi can tell a proxied user write from entire-api's own trail
494	//     merge; only the latter may bypass server-side-merge-only (COR-1916).
495	//     Keep it out of svcTokRepoReadWorkloads: a proxied request must never
496	//     be authorized cert-only.
497	//   - agent-insights is absent on purpose: it reads with installation tokens
