624	// svcTokGitAuthMiddleware builds the HTTP middleware that gates git
625	// smart-HTTP routes mounted on the svctok :8281 listener. Mirrors the
626	// public :443 git-auth chain (server/http.go:226's httpAuthMiddleware
627	// with auth.AcceptGitAuth) MINUS the jwtHasServiceSubject reject —
628	// service-identity tokens are exactly the expected shape on this
629	// surface (the "split-listener policy" documented at server/http.go:259
630	// says service callers belong on the internal mTLS listener). Workload
631	// identity is enforced one layer up by svctokserver.WorkloadGate, so
632	// this middleware focuses on Bearer JWT verification + the
633	// AcceptGitAuth kind policy.
634	//
635	// Cert-only exception: requests with no Authorization header from a workload
636	// this server authorizes cert-only (docs/auth.md §3.2) skip JWT verification
637	// entirely — the cert handshake is the whole authority and the middleware
638	// synthesises an internal workload principal via certOnlyGitPrincipal:
639	//
640	//   - WorkloadEntireDB — DISS catchup/repair peer fetches (PermitsGit pull
641	//     cluster-wide, push rejected). No STS round-trip to mint a per-fetch JWT.
642	//   - svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads (peregrine) — read-any-repo class (pull
643	//     cluster-wide, push rejected), identical shape to WorkloadEntireDB above.
644	//   - svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads (mirror-worker) — mirror-sync pushes
645	//     (write-mirror class: pull cluster-wide, push to mirror-class repos).
646	//
647	// Other workloads on this listener (entire-backup) continue to require a
648	// Bearer JWT.
649	func svcTokGitAuthMiddleware(trustDomain string, verifier *auth.IssuerVerifier) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
650		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
651			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
652				ctx := r.Context()
653	
654				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
655				if authHeader == "" {
656					if certOnly, ok := certOnlyGitPrincipal(r, trustDomain); ok {
657						// The bearer path stamps the principal on the span inside
658						// AuthenticateToken. This path has no token, so stamp it
659						// here, or mirror-sync and DISS traffic read as anonymous
660						// in every per-kind or per-handle view of git spans.
661						trace.SpanFromContext(ctx).SetAttributes(auth.PrincipalAttributes(certOnly)...)
662						ctx = reqctx.SetPrincipal(ctx, certOnly)
663						ctx = reqctx.SetAuthSource(ctx, reqctx.AuthSourceMTLS)
664						next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
665						return
666					}
667					w.Header().Set("WWW-Authenticate", `Basic realm="Entire Git Server"`)
668					w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
669					_, _ = w.Write([]byte("Missing Authorization header")) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort error response
670					return
671				}
672	
673				// git over HTTP sends the JWT as the Basic-Auth password.
674				token, ok := auth.BearerOrBasicToken(r)
675				if !ok {
676					w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
677					_, _ = w.Write([]byte("Invalid Authorization header format")) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort error response
678					return
679				}
680	
681				principal, _, err := auth.AuthenticateToken(ctx, verifier, token)
682				if err != nil {
683					slogutil.Debug(ctx, "svctok git auth failed", slog.Any("error", err))
684					w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
685					_, _ = w.Write([]byte("Invalid or expired token")) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort error response
686					return
687				}
688	
689				if !auth.AcceptGitAuth(principal.Kind) {
690					slogutil.Warn(ctx, "svctok git token kind not permitted",
691						slog.String("kind", string(principal.Kind)),
692						slog.String("path", r.URL.Path))
693					w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
694					_, _ = w.Write([]byte("Token not valid for this endpoint")) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort error response
695					return
696				}
697	
698				ctx = reqctx.SetPrincipal(ctx, principal)
699				ctx = reqctx.SetRawToken(ctx, token)
700				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
701			})
702		}
703	}

705	// svcTokRepoAPIAuthMiddleware gates the huma repo-API routes mounted on the
706	// svctok :8281 listener. Mirrors the public :443 repo-API chain
707	// (server/http.go's httpRepoAuthMiddleware → AcceptRepoAPIAuth) MINUS the
708	// jwtHasServiceSubject reject — service-identity tokens are the expected
709	// shape here (workload identity is enforced one layer up by WorkloadGate).
710	// Errors render as problem+json via the supplied huma.API for parity with the
711	// public mount. AuthenticateToken runs the RFC 8705 §3 cnf check against the
712	// peer leaf stashed by withPeerLeaf, binding a cnf-carrying token to the cert;
713	// on this mTLS channel a confidential-client/service token (repo-scoped,
714	// service:entiredb) with no cnf is rejected (the strict-cnf flip), so cert
715	// binding and WorkloadGate both gate that Bearer path. A forwarded account
716	// access bearer (including the OBO shape) is cnf-less by design and exempt
717	// from that check (docs/auth.md §3.1) — see AuthenticateToken.
718	//
719	// Cert-only branch: a request from a svcTokRepoReadWorkloads workload with no
720	// Authorization header skips token verification entirely. The cert is the
721	// whole credential (docs/auth.md §3.2): the middleware synthesises a
722	// reqctx.KindInternalWorkload principal (pull cluster-wide, push rejected) from
723	// the mTLS leaf, with no Bearer and no SpiceDB lookup. A user-originated read
724	// instead arrives with a forwarded account access bearer (cnf-less, the
725	// entire-api content read-through shape), so it takes the Bearer
726	// path below and is authorized live on sub against SpiceDB. Other admitted
727	// workloads (entire-mcp, entire-search) also present a Bearer.
728	func svcTokRepoAPIAuthMiddleware(trustDomain string, verifier *auth.IssuerVerifier) repoapi.AuthMiddleware {
729		return func(api huma.API, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
730			writeErr := func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, status int, msg string) {
731				_ = huma.WriteErr(api, humago.NewContext(nil, r, w), status, msg) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort auth error response
732			}
733			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
734				ctx := r.Context()
735				if r.Header.Get("Authorization") == "" {
736					if repoRead, ok := internalWorkloadFromCert(r, trustDomain, svcTokRepoReadWorkloads...); ok {
737						ctx = reqctx.SetPrincipal(ctx, repoRead)
738						ctx = reqctx.SetAuthSource(ctx, reqctx.AuthSourceMTLS)
739						next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
740						return
741					}
742					writeErr(w, r, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Missing Authorization header")
743					return
744				}
745				token, ok := auth.BearerOrBasicToken(r)
746				if !ok {
747					writeErr(w, r, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Invalid Authorization header format")
748					return
749				}
750				principal, _, err := auth.AuthenticateToken(ctx, verifier, token)
751				if err != nil {
752					slogutil.Debug(ctx, "svctok repo-api auth failed", slog.Any("error", err))
753					writeErr(w, r, http.StatusUnauthorized, "Invalid or expired token")
754					return
755				}
756				if !auth.AcceptRepoAPIAuth(principal.Kind) {
757					slogutil.Warn(ctx, "svctok repo-api token kind not permitted",
758						slog.String("kind", string(principal.Kind)),
759						slog.String("path", r.URL.Path))
760					writeErr(w, r, http.StatusForbidden, "Token not valid for this endpoint")
761					return
762				}
763				ctx = reqctx.SetPrincipal(ctx, principal)
764				ctx = reqctx.SetRawToken(ctx, token)
765				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
766			})
767		}
768	}

770	// certOnlyGitPrincipal synthesises the cert-only principal for the git mounts.
771	// Three allowlists meet here (docs/auth.md §3.2): entiredb peers and
772	// svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads (peregrine) get the read-only class unchanged,
773	// and svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads additionally get WriteMirror set, which lets
774	// PermitsGit authorize push (receive-pack narrows it to mirror-class repos).
775	// The caller is resolved once — unlike internalWorkloadFromCert's per-allowlist
776	// check, checking three allowlists against one resolved caller avoids
777	// re-parsing the peer cert (and re-logging callerFromMTLS's rejection warning)
778	// once per allowlist.
779	//
780	// svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads is checked before svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads so a
781	// workload accidentally listed in both gets the more privileged grant rather
782	// than being silently downgraded to read-only by switch-case order; today the
783	// two allowlists are disjoint, so this ordering is not load-bearing yet.
784	func certOnlyGitPrincipal(r *http.Request, trustDomain string) (reqctx.Principal, bool) {
785		caller, ok := svctokserver.CallerFromMTLS(r, trustDomain)
786		if !ok {
787			return reqctx.Principal{}, false
788		}
789		workload, known := servicetoken.WorkloadFromSAN(caller.Name)
790		if !known {
791			return reqctx.Principal{}, false
792		}
793		p := reqctx.Principal{Handle: string(workload), Kind: reqctx.KindInternalWorkload}
794		switch {
795		case slices.Contains(svcTokWriteMirrorWorkloads, workload):
796			p.WriteMirror = true
797			return p, true
798		case workload == servicetoken.WorkloadEntireDB, slices.Contains(svcTokReadAnyRepoWorkloads, workload):
799			return p, true
800		default:
801			return reqctx.Principal{}, false
802		}
803	}

805	// internalWorkloadFromCert synthesises a cert-only internal workload principal
806	// when the inbound peer cert resolves to one of the allowed workloads. Returns
807	// ok=false for any other shape — no peer cert, wrong trust domain, or a
808	// workload not on the caller's allowlist. The cert chain is already validated
809	// by the TLS handshake and the workload narrowed by svctokserver.WorkloadGate
810	// one layer up; passing the per-surface allowlist here turns that identity into
811	// a static permission class with no Bearer and no SpiceDB lookup (docs/auth.md
812	// §3.2). The principal carries no account: an internal workload is not a
813	// SpiceDB account, and the peer's SPIFFE identity (recorded by WorkloadGate) is
814	// the audit subject. Handle names the workload so request logs attribute it.
815	// CallerFromMTLS requires a positive SPIFFE claim, so entiredb is classified
816	// from the workload URI SAN its EC2 cert carries.
817	func internalWorkloadFromCert(r *http.Request, trustDomain string, allowed ...servicetoken.Workload) (reqctx.Principal, bool) {
818		caller, ok := svctokserver.CallerFromMTLS(r, trustDomain)
819		if !ok {
820			return reqctx.Principal{}, false
821		}
822		workload, known := servicetoken.WorkloadFromSAN(caller.Name)
823		if !known || !slices.Contains(allowed, workload) {
824			return reqctx.Principal{}, false
825		}
826		return reqctx.Principal{
827			Handle: string(workload),
828			Kind:   reqctx.KindInternalWorkload,
829		}, true
830	}

229	// serveAuthenticatedGit is the shared tail of handleRepo and
230	// handleRepoByULIDAuth: capability check via resolveRepoLoader, then
231	// dispatch to the matching git smart-HTTP handler. repoSlug is the
232	// audience-style URL slug for this route (the path under /git/ that
233	// the route resolved); passed through to PermitsGit so the comparison
234	// stays in slug terms rather than ULID terms.
235	func (s *Service) serveAuthenticatedGit(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, repoID repositories.ID, repoSlug string) {
236		ctx := r.Context()
237	
238		// Restore-mode flip: a backup-restore JWT carries RestoreMode=true,
239		// signalling that the receive-pack flow is replaying refs from a
240		// backup bundle and the recording decorator should NOT re-emit RSL/
241		// NATS entries for them. Replaces the legacy X-Entire-Api-Auth-triggered
242		// restore mode in handleRepoByID — same effect, JWT-claim-driven instead
243		// of header-driven. Gated on Kind==TokenBackupAccess so a stray
244		// RestoreMode bit on any other kind (e.g. a future claimsFromJWT
245		// drift) cannot quietly suppress recording.
246		if p, ok := reqctx.GetPrincipal(ctx); ok && isRestorePrincipal(p) {
247			ctx = refstore.ContextWithRestoreMode(ctx)
248			r = r.WithContext(ctx)
249		}
250	
251		loader, err := s.resolveRepoLoader(ctx, repoID, repoSlug, gitutil.SmartHTTPOp(r))
252		if err != nil {
253			if hErr, ok := errors.AsType[*httpError](err); ok {
254				// Render through http.Error so the enumeration-guard 404 from
255				// resolveRepoLoader is byte-identical (status, Content-Type,
256				// nosniff, trailing newline) to handleRepo's unknown-slug 404.
257				// Any divergence between the two 404s would itself be an oracle.
258				msg := hErr.message
259				if msg == "" {
260					msg = http.StatusText(hErr.status)
261				}
262				http.Error(w, msg, hErr.status)
263			} else {
264				slogutil.Error(ctx, "Unexpected error serving git request", slog.Any("error", err))
265				http.Error(w, http.StatusText(http.StatusInternalServerError), http.StatusInternalServerError)
266			}
267			return
268		}
269		defer func() { _ = loader.Storage().Close() }()
270	
271		if isInfoRefsDiscovery(r) {
272			// git prints the body of a failed ref discovery but not the body of a
273			// failed receive-pack POST, so the freeze is refused here first to
274			// show the user why. The POST check below stays authoritative.
275			if r.URL.Query().Get("service") == transport.ReceivePackService {
276				principal, _ := reqctx.GetPrincipal(ctx)
277				if !isMirrorWorker(principal) {
278					repoRow, _, err := s.fetchRepoRow(ctx, repoID)
279					if err != nil {
280						slogutil.Error(ctx, "repo state lookup failed", slog.String("repo_id", repoID.String()), slog.Any("error", err))
281						http.Error(w, "repo state lookup unavailable, retry later", http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
282						return
283					}
284					if refuseFrozenWrite(ctx, w, principal, repoRow, repoID) {
285						return
286					}
287				}
288			}
289			// Mount-aware addr pool — public mount uses each provider's public
290			// HTTPAddr; svctok mount uses HTTPInternalAddr (ADR 20260518). When
291			// internal-addr is configured but no peer has gossiped one yet
292			// (mid-rollout), HTTPInternalAddrs returns empty and the discovery
293			// helper returns false → falls through to the local handler with
294			// DissStore-backed object fetch.
295			var addrs []string
296			if s.UseInternalAddr {
297				addrs = loader.Storage().HTTPInternalAddrs()
298			} else {
299				addrs = loader.Storage().HTTPAddrs()
300			}
301			// Three-tier ordering, all GET /info/refs:
302			//   1. HandleInfoRefsDiscovery — sets X-Entire-Replicas and 307s
303			//      to a hosting replica when this node doesn't host the
304			//      repo (or always for ALB-routed traffic). Must run first
305			//      so v2 clients still get the replica redirect.
306			//   2. serveV2InfoRefs — emits the v2 capability advertisement
307			//      when the client sent `Git-Protocol: version=2` AND a
308			//      V2Registry is configured. Must run BEFORE HandleInfoRefs
309			//      because that handler returns true for every
310			//      service=git-upload-pack request and would otherwise
311			//      consume the v2 client's request as v0/v1.
312			//   3. HandleInfoRefs — v0/v1 advertisement (the default). We
313			//      override go-git's AdvertiseRefs here because upstream
314			//      omits the object-format capability on receive-pack,
315			//      which makes real git clients abort SHA256 pushes with
316			//      "the receiving end does not support this repository's
317			//      hash algorithm".
318			if s.HandleInfoRefsDiscovery(w, r, addrs) {
319				if adminapi.IsShuttingDown(s.Shutdown) {
320					emitStepdownRedirected(r, "infoRefs")
321				}
322				return
323			}
324			// Declined while draining means no replica was available to take the
325			// client, and advertising refs here would promise a pack this node
326			// will not serve.
327			if adminapi.IsShuttingDown(s.Shutdown) {
328				assert.Reachable("infoRefs: rejected during shutdown with 503", nil)
329				emitStepdownRejected(r, "infoRefs")
330				http.Error(w, "node is shutting down", http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
331				return
332			}
333			if s.serveV2InfoRefs(w, r, loader.Storage()) {
334				return
335			}
336			if HandleInfoRefs(w, r, loader.Storage(), HideRefsFrom(s.refPolicyResolver())) {
337				return
338			}

1	# Native mirroring across clusters
2	
3	Status: Accepted (v1 scope updated 2026-07-22; partially superseded —
4	[20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md](./20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md) changes the
5	git-data primary once, at detach)
6	
7	## TLDR
8	
9	A native repo today lives in exactly one cluster. This ADR gives it read-only
10	**native mirror** placements in other clusters, replicated through the existing
11	GitHub-mirror pipeline. The primary stays the single source of truth: every
12	push lands there, ref events fan sync jobs to each native mirror's cluster, and the
13	same mirror-worker fetches from the primary and pushes into the native mirror.
14	Native mirrors reject user pushes, inherit read authorization from the primary
15	through the shared SpiceDB graph, and are created/torn down asynchronously by
16	a reconciler owned by the target jurisdiction.
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	GitHub mirrors are already multi-placement: one upstream, N per-cluster
21	placements, unified by a repo group, synced by mirror-pipeline
22	(`mirror_git_v1` jobs consumed by a per-cluster worker that does a generic
23	git fetch/push). Native repos are singleton placements, but the groundwork
24	anticipated this feature: every repo has a group (ADR
25	20260715-repo-group-for-every-repo), the group's `forge_repo_id` for an
26	`entire` group is "the initial placement; later it may be the canonical data
27	primary", the mirror job schema reserves `SourceKind = "entiredb"`, and the
28	data plane emits a transactional-outbox ref event (`repo_refs_v1`) on every
29	ref change. mirror-pipeline's multi-region design docs sketched this as
30	"stage 2" before `repo_refs_v1` existed.
31	
32	## Decision
33	
34	> **Partially superseded by [20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md](./20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md).**
35	> The git-data primary is no longer immutable: a detach moves it from the
36	> GitHub upstream to the detached placement, once. The `Primaries` contract
37	> comment in `core/resourceevents` records this.
38	
39	**Identity & primary.** A native mirror is a new placement of the primary's
40	existing `entire` repo group, with its own placement ULID. The git-data
41	primary remains `repo_group.forge_repo_id` — immutable in v1. The global
42	registry gains a `placement_role`; the per-project name-uniqueness index is
43	scoped to primaries, and logical-repo reads (by-name, project listings)
44	resolve primaries only, with native mirrors surfaced via `Placements[]`. Native-mirror
45	placements are owned by the primary's project in CRDB only. The first
46	native mirror activates the group's dormant identity: the primary's data-plane row
47	is stamped with the group id (so ref events carry it) and the entire-api
48	projection is converged (group + processing-primary flag), without which the
49	facts-emission gate suppresses the primary.
50	
51	**Replication.** Reuse the mirror pipeline unchanged at the transport layer:
52	`sync_repo` jobs on each target cluster's `mirror_git_v1` with
53	`SourceKind=entiredb` and a Core-computed internal source URL; the worker
54	fetches from the primary's svctok listener (its cert-only cluster-wide pull
55	already covers this) and pushes locally. The trigger is a fanout consumer on
56	the local `repo_refs_v1` stream, with loop prevention (drop unless the local
57	cluster is the group's home). `repo_refs_v1` is a lossy notification bus. v1
58	is event-driven only: every sync carries full ref state, so the next primary
59	push heals a lost event, but an idle repo can remain stale indefinitely. A
60	per-cluster resync sweep and a fixed staleness RPO are deferred to Phase 6.
61	The initial seed is the same job, published at creation; operators can
62	hand-publish that job as the v1 recovery escape hatch.
63	
64	**Authorization.** The native mirror's SpiceDB object is a bare node carrying
65	exactly one relation, `canonical_primary`. Read permissions (`pull`, `list`,
66	`view_metadata`) inherit through it; there are no native mirror-local write/admin
67	arms and no `project`/`platform` edges (those would confer `push`/`manage`
68	via project arrows and bypass every guard). Grants, revocations, and
69	visibility changes on the primary therefore apply to native mirrors at
70	read-native mirror staleness with no state copying — SpiceDB is one logical
71	cluster behind the shared authz-writer. Denials keep the platform's
72	enumeration-guard posture: on deny, resolve the placement role and
73	re-authorize against the primary; only a caller authorized on the primary
74	sees a native mirror-specific error (with the primary's public URL). Token
75	exchange resolves placements by audience host so native mirror-host clones work.
76	Authority mutations (grants, visibility, service accounts, CI) are rejected
77	on native mirror ULIDs; authority-inspection reads resolve to the primary.
78	Moving permissions and project assignment onto the repo group is the desired
79	long-term convergence shape, but is a separate migration (COR-1040/COR-1041)
80	and does not gate v1.
81	
82	**Write posture.** Native mirrors hard-reject user pushes. The data-plane
83	receive-pack gate is defense-in-depth; the user-visible rejection happens at
84	token minting and the core APIs. Only the mirror-worker's write-mirror
85	class may push native-mirror storage (`IsMirror() || IsNativeMirror()`).
86	
87	> **Amended 2026-09-23 (COR-1895).** The write posture above describes the
88	> original v1 decision. It no longer matches the shipped behaviour. A
89	> `git push` to a native-mirror placement is forwarded to the primary
90	> (COR-1350), and the primary re-authorizes the caller and applies its own ref
91	> protection. Token minting does not reject the push. It authorizes the action
92	> against the primary, which the repo URL resolves to, and then scopes the
93	> token to the placement for the mirror host. In SpiceDB, the `repo#group`
94	> edge (COR-1589) also gives the placement the group's `push`. Only the
95	> mirror worker writes the placement's local storage. The repo API still refuses its own write
96	> capabilities on a placement, because it does not forward them. That
97	> refusal names the API, not the repo.
98	
99	**Lifecycle.** Creation is asynchronous: the primary jurisdiction's core
100	validates the target (existing, native mirror-hosting, cross-jurisdiction in v1),
101	activates the group, and writes a durable intent row (`native_mirrors`:
102	stage machine `pending → provisioned → registered → seeded → announced`,
103	snapshotted immutable params — notably `object_format` — plus lease and
104	retry fields), then returns 202. The **target** jurisdiction's lifecycle
105	reconciler executes the tail — regional bridges only contain their own
106	jurisdiction's clusters — claiming rows via a row lease with fenced,
107	CAS'd transitions (CockroachDB has no advisory locks). Deletion flips
108	`desired_state` and always wins: a failed CAS re-reads and runs the
109	idempotent teardown leg only when deletion is intended. Primary deletion
110	while native mirrors exist is rejected on interactive paths (tombstone
111	set/checked/cleared in one locked transaction; retained through accepted
112	zero-native mirror deletions); account erasure cascades mirror-first through the
113	shared finalizer's caller modes, returning retryable until native mirror rows are
114	gone.
115	
116	The v1 reconciler keeps retryable backoff, row-lease reclamation, fenced stage
117	resume, and idempotent teardown. Permanent-error classification, attempts
118	caps, suspension/resume polish, operator recovery controls, and exhaustive
119	chaos testing are Phase 6 work. The public create/status/delete API is the
120	operator surface through `entire api`; a dedicated CLI is not required for v1.

# Native mirroring across clusters

Status: Accepted (v1 scope updated 2026-07-22; partially superseded —
[20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md](./20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md) changes the
git-data primary once, at detach)

## TLDR

A native repo today lives in exactly one cluster. This ADR gives it read-only
**native mirror** placements in other clusters, replicated through the existing
GitHub-mirror pipeline. The primary stays the single source of truth: every
push lands there, ref events fan sync jobs to each native mirror's cluster, and the
same mirror-worker fetches from the primary and pushes into the native mirror.
Native mirrors reject user pushes, inherit read authorization from the primary
through the shared SpiceDB graph, and are created/torn down asynchronously by
a reconciler owned by the target jurisdiction.

## Context

GitHub mirrors are already multi-placement: one upstream, N per-cluster
placements, unified by a repo group, synced by mirror-pipeline
(`mirror_git_v1` jobs consumed by a per-cluster worker that does a generic
git fetch/push). Native repos are singleton placements, but the groundwork
anticipated this feature: every repo has a group (ADR
20260715-repo-group-for-every-repo), the group's `forge_repo_id` for an
`entire` group is "the initial placement; later it may be the canonical data
primary", the mirror job schema reserves `SourceKind = "entiredb"`, and the
data plane emits a transactional-outbox ref event (`repo_refs_v1`) on every
ref change. mirror-pipeline's multi-region design docs sketched this as
"stage 2" before `repo_refs_v1` existed.

## Decision

> **Partially superseded by [20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md](./20260930-detach-github-mirror-same-cell.md).**
> The git-data primary is no longer immutable: a detach moves it from the
> GitHub upstream to the detached placement, once. The `Primaries` contract
> comment in `core/resourceevents` records this.

**Identity & primary.** A native mirror is a new placement of the primary's
existing `entire` repo group, with its own placement ULID. The git-data
primary remains `repo_group.forge_repo_id` — immutable in v1. The global
registry gains a `placement_role`; the per-project name-uniqueness index is
scoped to primaries, and logical-repo reads (by-name, project listings)
resolve primaries only, with native mirrors surfaced via `Placements[]`. Native-mirror
placements are owned by the primary's project in CRDB only. The first
native mirror activates the group's dormant identity: the primary's data-plane row
is stamped with the group id (so ref events carry it) and the entire-api
projection is converged (group + processing-primary flag), without which the
facts-emission gate suppresses the primary.

**Replication.** Reuse the mirror pipeline unchanged at the transport layer:
`sync_repo` jobs on each target cluster's `mirror_git_v1` with
`SourceKind=entiredb` and a Core-computed internal source URL; the worker
fetches from the primary's svctok listener (its cert-only cluster-wide pull
already covers this) and pushes locally. The trigger is a fanout consumer on
the local `repo_refs_v1` stream, with loop prevention (drop unless the local
cluster is the group's home). `repo_refs_v1` is a lossy notification bus. v1
is event-driven only: every sync carries full ref state, so the next primary
push heals a lost event, but an idle repo can remain stale indefinitely. A
per-cluster resync sweep and a fixed staleness RPO are deferred to Phase 6.
The initial seed is the same job, published at creation; operators can
hand-publish that job as the v1 recovery escape hatch.

**Authorization.** The native mirror's SpiceDB object is a bare node carrying
exactly one relation, `canonical_primary`. Read permissions (`pull`, `list`,
`view_metadata`) inherit through it; there are no native mirror-local write/admin
arms and no `project`/`platform` edges (those would confer `push`/`manage`
via project arrows and bypass every guard). Grants, revocations, and
visibility changes on the primary therefore apply to native mirrors at
read-native mirror staleness with no state copying — SpiceDB is one logical
cluster behind the shared authz-writer. Denials keep the platform's
enumeration-guard posture: on deny, resolve the placement role and
re-authorize against the primary; only a caller authorized on the primary
sees a native mirror-specific error (with the primary's public URL). Token
exchange resolves placements by audience host so native mirror-host clones work.
Authority mutations (grants, visibility, service accounts, CI) are rejected
on native mirror ULIDs; authority-inspection reads resolve to the primary.
Moving permissions and project assignment onto the repo group is the desired
long-term convergence shape, but is a separate migration (COR-1040/COR-1041)
and does not gate v1.

**Write posture.** Native mirrors hard-reject user pushes. The data-plane
receive-pack gate is defense-in-depth; the user-visible rejection happens at
token minting and the core APIs. Only the mirror-worker's write-mirror
class may push native-mirror storage (`IsMirror() || IsNativeMirror()`).

> **Amended 2026-09-23 (COR-1895).** The write posture above describes the
> original v1 decision. It no longer matches the shipped behaviour. A
> `git push` to a native-mirror placement is forwarded to the primary
> (COR-1350), and the primary re-authorizes the caller and applies its own ref
> protection. Token minting does not reject the push. It authorizes the action
> against the primary, which the repo URL resolves to, and then scopes the
> token to the placement for the mirror host. In SpiceDB, the `repo#group`
> edge (COR-1589) also gives the placement the group's `push`. Only the
> mirror worker writes the placement's local storage. The repo API still refuses its own write
> capabilities on a placement, because it does not forward them. That
> refusal names the API, not the repo.

**Lifecycle.** Creation is asynchronous: the primary jurisdiction's core
validates the target (existing, native mirror-hosting, cross-jurisdiction in v1),
activates the group, and writes a durable intent row (`native_mirrors`:
stage machine `pending → provisioned → registered → seeded → announced`,
snapshotted immutable params — notably `object_format` — plus lease and
retry fields), then returns 202. The **target** jurisdiction's lifecycle
reconciler executes the tail — regional bridges only contain their own
jurisdiction's clusters — claiming rows via a row lease with fenced,
CAS'd transitions (CockroachDB has no advisory locks). Deletion flips
`desired_state` and always wins: a failed CAS re-reads and runs the
idempotent teardown leg only when deletion is intended. Primary deletion
while native mirrors exist is rejected on interactive paths (tombstone
set/checked/cleared in one locked transaction; retained through accepted
zero-native mirror deletions); account erasure cascades mirror-first through the
shared finalizer's caller modes, returning retryable until native mirror rows are
gone.

The v1 reconciler keeps retryable backoff, row-lease reclamation, fenced stage
resume, and idempotent teardown. Permanent-error classification, attempts
caps, suspension/resume polish, operator recovery controls, and exhaustive
chaos testing are Phase 6 work. The public create/status/delete API is the
operator surface through `entire api`; a dedicated CLI is not required for v1.

## Consequences

- Native mirrors are read-only, near-line copies: clone/fetch locally, push to the
  primary. The normal ref-event path converges in seconds; after a lost event,
  the v1 staleness bound is the primary's next push (or an operator-published
  sync job), not a fixed cadence.
- v1 scope: cross-jurisdiction native mirrors only; primary migration, push-through
  to the primary, settings-parity guarantees for new placements, repo-rename
  URL propagation to native-mirror clusters, and same-jurisdiction placements are
  deliberately deferred.
- The mirror pipeline's failure machinery (failure index, rekicker,
  done-events) is inherited as-is; native mirror status is driven by the same
  completion events through a composite writer gated on the intent's stage
  and desired state.
- The worker admits only `svctok.<single-cluster-label>.<environment-domain>:8281`
  sources, fails closed when the environment domain is unavailable, and keys
  per-sync mTLS routing off that admitted parent. Pairwise SG ingress is the
  v1 cluster boundary. Authoritative worker-side verification of the source
  repo → target placement pair is deferred hardening.
- Automatic cross-jurisdiction repo-token routing is deferred (COR-1043).
  v1 users authenticate in the target jurisdiction before cloning a native
  mirror.

> **Amended 2026-09-23 (COR-1895).** Two consequences above are stale.
> Push-through to the primary shipped (see the write-posture amendment), so
> native mirrors are not read-only for `git push`: their local storage is
> read-only, and git writes are forwarded. COR-1043 is Done in Linear, and
> the COR-1895 audit cloned a US native mirror with an EU login on staging.
> Check the current token-routing behaviour before relying on the COR-1043
> deferral above.

## RSL trust readiness and future promotion

The RSL root-of-trust MVP (ADR 20260724) eagerly includes every native
placement's cluster signer in repository policy and requires a destination-local
trust acceptance receipt. This makes an accepted mirror cryptographically ready
for a future takeover without an emergency root-key operation against a dead
primary. It does **not** change this ADR's v1 write posture: the
`repo_group.forge_repo_id` primary remains immutable, mirrors remain read-only,
and their authorized local RSL signers remain unused.

Actual leader promotion is a separate follow-up that must supersede or extend
this ADR. It requires a monotonic leadership generation and durable stale-writer
fence, write-token and routing cutover, replication-direction reversal, a final
sync when the old primary is reachable or explicit acknowledgement of the
selected mirror's staleness/RPO when it is not, and quarantine/forward recovery
for a returning old primary with divergent writes. Only after the new leader
has a current trust acceptance receipt and its local signer remains authorized
may it append its first locally signed RSL entry, descending from the selected
accepted primary-produced RSL tip.

76	Authority mutations (grants, visibility, service accounts, CI) are rejected
77	on native mirror ULIDs; authority-inspection reads resolve to the primary.
78	Moving permissions and project assignment onto the repo group is the desired
79	long-term convergence shape, but is a separate migration (COR-1040/COR-1041)
80	and does not gate v1.
81	
82	**Write posture.** Native mirrors hard-reject user pushes. The data-plane
83	receive-pack gate is defense-in-depth; the user-visible rejection happens at
84	token minting and the core APIs. Only the mirror-worker's write-mirror
85	class may push native-mirror storage (`IsMirror() || IsNativeMirror()`).
86	
87	> **Amended 2026-09-23 (COR-1895).** The write posture above describes the
88	> original v1 decision. It no longer matches the shipped behaviour. A
89	> `git push` to a native-mirror placement is forwarded to the primary
90	> (COR-1350), and the primary re-authorizes the caller and applies its own ref
91	> protection. Token minting does not reject the push. It authorizes the action
92	> against the primary, which the repo URL resolves to, and then scopes the
93	> token to the placement for the mirror host. In SpiceDB, the `repo#group`
94	> edge (COR-1589) also gives the placement the group's `push`. Only the
95	> mirror worker writes the placement's local storage. The repo API still refuses its own write
96	> capabilities on a placement, because it does not forward them. That
97	> refusal names the API, not the repo.
98	
99	**Lifecycle.** Creation is asynchronous: the primary jurisdiction's core
100	validates the target (existing, native mirror-hosting, cross-jurisdiction in v1),
101	activates the group, and writes a durable intent row (`native_mirrors`:
102	stage machine `pending → provisioned → registered → seeded → announced`,
103	snapshotted immutable params — notably `object_format` — plus lease and
104	retry fields), then returns 202. The **target** jurisdiction's lifecycle
105	reconciler executes the tail — regional bridges only contain their own
106	jurisdiction's clusters — claiming rows via a row lease with fenced,
107	CAS'd transitions (CockroachDB has no advisory locks). Deletion flips
108	`desired_state` and always wins: a failed CAS re-reads and runs the
109	idempotent teardown leg only when deletion is intended. Primary deletion
110	while native mirrors exist is rejected on interactive paths (tombstone
111	set/checked/cleared in one locked transaction; retained through accepted
112	zero-native mirror deletions); account erasure cascades mirror-first through the
113	shared finalizer's caller modes, returning retryable until native mirror rows are
114	gone.
115	
116	The v1 reconciler keeps retryable backoff, row-lease reclamation, fenced stage
117	resume, and idempotent teardown. Permanent-error classification, attempts
118	caps, suspension/resume polish, operator recovery controls, and exhaustive
119	chaos testing are Phase 6 work. The public create/status/delete API is the
120	operator surface through `entire api`; a dedicated CLI is not required for v1.
121	
122	## Consequences
123	
124	- Native mirrors are read-only, near-line copies: clone/fetch locally, push to the
125	  primary. The normal ref-event path converges in seconds; after a lost event,
126	  the v1 staleness bound is the primary's next push (or an operator-published
127	  sync job), not a fixed cadence.
128	- v1 scope: cross-jurisdiction native mirrors only; primary migration, push-through
129	  to the primary, settings-parity guarantees for new placements, repo-rename
130	  URL propagation to native-mirror clusters, and same-jurisdiction placements are
131	  deliberately deferred.
132	- The mirror pipeline's failure machinery (failure index, rekicker,
133	  done-events) is inherited as-is; native mirror status is driven by the same
134	  completion events through a composite writer gated on the intent's stage
135	  and desired state.
136	- The worker admits only `svctok.<single-cluster-label>.<environment-domain>:8281`
137	  sources, fails closed when the environment domain is unavailable, and keys
138	  per-sync mTLS routing off that admitted parent. Pairwise SG ingress is the
139	  v1 cluster boundary. Authoritative worker-side verification of the source
140	  repo → target placement pair is deferred hardening.
141	- Automatic cross-jurisdiction repo-token routing is deferred (COR-1043).
142	  v1 users authenticate in the target jurisdiction before cloning a native
143	  mirror.
144	
145	> **Amended 2026-09-23 (COR-1895).** Two consequences above are stale.
146	> Push-through to the primary shipped (see the write-posture amendment), so
147	> native mirrors are not read-only for `git push`: their local storage is
148	> read-only, and git writes are forwarded. COR-1043 is Done in Linear, and
149	> the COR-1895 audit cloned a US native mirror with an EU login on staging.
150	> Check the current token-routing behaviour before relying on the COR-1043
151	> deferral above.
152	
153	## RSL trust readiness and future promotion
154	
155	The RSL root-of-trust MVP (ADR 20260724) eagerly includes every native
156	placement's cluster signer in repository policy and requires a destination-local
157	trust acceptance receipt. This makes an accepted mirror cryptographically ready
158	for a future takeover without an emergency root-key operation against a dead
159	primary. It does **not** change this ADR's v1 write posture: the
160	`repo_group.forge_repo_id` primary remains immutable, mirrors remain read-only,
161	and their authorized local RSL signers remain unused.
162	
163	Actual leader promotion is a separate follow-up that must supersede or extend
164	this ADR. It requires a monotonic leadership generation and durable stale-writer
165	fence, write-token and routing cutover, replication-direction reversal, a final
166	sync when the old primary is reachable or explicit acknowledgement of the
167	selected mirror's staleness/RPO when it is not, and quarantine/forward recovery
168	for a returning old primary with divergent writes. Only after the new leader
169	has a current trust acceptance receipt and its local signer remains authorized
170	may it append its first locally signed RSL entry, descending from the selected
171	accepted primary-produced RSL tip.

263	//     one. A repository this creates is made crash-safe by the driver's Init;
264	//     one that already existed is not, which is the gap this closes — git does
265	//     not fsync loose objects by default, so a crash can keep a ref and lose the
266	//     object it names, and Check exists to find exactly that. Three callers wrote this
267	//     sequence out and two of them left the crash-safety line out of it.
268	//
269	//   - The remote before the announcement, because announcing fetches from it.
270	//
271	//   - The announcement last, because it is the one step that needs the
272	//     network. It announces this writer against a view of what the store has
273	//     already folded, so the low-water mark it promises is not below finished
274	//     work — everything after it is offline. Only when there is a remote: a
275	//     store nobody shares needs no announcement, and a writer announced earlier
276	//     than it writes holds the barrier further back than it has to.
277	//
278	// Idempotent, so an application may call it every time it starts: the repository
279	// is created only if absent, an announcement returns early if this writer has
280	// one, and the crash-safety settings are the same two config writes either way.
281	//
282	// A store that is only going to be read wants Open. An announced writer that
283	// never writes holds the barrier where it stood.
284	func Prepare(d git.Driver, tp git.Transport, repoDir, name string, config settings.Settings, originURL string) (*Store, error) {
285		if _, err := d.Open(repoDir); err != nil {
286			if _, err := d.Init(repoDir, git.InitOptions{}); err != nil {
287				return nil, err
288			}
289		}
290		s, err := Open(d, tp, repoDir, name, config)
291		if err != nil {
292			return nil, err
293		}
294		remote, err := s.remote()
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		if remote == "" {
299			remote = defaultRemote
300		}
301		if originURL != "" {
302			if err := s.Configure(remote, originURL); err != nil {
303				return nil, err
304			}
305		}
306		if err := s.repo.MakeCrashSafe(); err != nil {
307			return nil, err
308		}
309		// What this store was created as, so a tool that follows a store rather than
310		// declaring one has something to read before the first generation records it.
311		if err := s.repo.ConfigSet(s.declaredKey(),
312			hex.EncodeToString(wire.EncodeSettings(config))); err != nil {
313			return nil, err
314		}
315		if originURL == "" {
316			return s, nil
317		}
318		if err := s.Announce(remote); err != nil {
319			return nil, err
320		}
321		return s, nil
322	}
323	
324	// defaultRemote is the name Prepare wires a URL under when the store has no
325	// remote yet; once it has one, renamed or not, Prepare keeps it. A caller that
326	// wants another name has Open, Configure and Announce, which is what Prepare is
327	// composed of.
328	const defaultRemote = "origin"
329	
330	// Writer returns this clone's writer identity.
331	func (s *Store) Writer() string { return s.writer }
332	
333	// Load derives state: the newest generation, then every op still held by every
334	// log.
335	//
336	// The ops are folded over the generation without filtering by boundary. That is
337	// safe and it is why compaction needs no bookkeeping about which ops it consumed:
338	// the fold is idempotent, and a generation already holds the winner for
339	// everything below its boundary, so re-folding those ops changes nothing. It also
340	// means an op that arrives late, below a boundary already published, is folded
341	// correctly rather than silently skipped — it simply loses on stamp, which is the
342	// right answer. What makes reads cheap is pruning the segments, not filtering
343	// them.
344	func (f *Follower) Load() (*record.State, []record.Conflict, error) {
345		return f.loadNarrowed(f.shape.Everything())
346	}

package multicellular

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/multicellular/events"
	"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/multicellular/harness"
)

func TestStrataWritesFromEveryCellLandInOneRepo(t *testing.T) {
	w := harness.New(t)
	us, eu := w.Jurisdiction("us").Cell("us-1"), w.Jurisdiction("eu").Cell("eu-1")
	repo := w.Repo()
	us.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	eu.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	w.Settle()

	us.AssertWriteAdmitted(us.API.CreatesStrataStore(repo))
	eu.SharesStrataRepoWith(us)
	eu.AssertWriteAdmitted(eu.API.CreatesStrataStore(repo))

	elected := time.Now().UTC()
	us.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	eu.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	w.Settle()

	us.AssertWriteAdmitted(us.API.WritesStrataEdits(repo))
	eu.AssertWriteAdmitted(eu.API.WritesStrataEdits(repo))
	us.AssertStrataPlanLanded()
	eu.AssertStrataPlanLanded()
}

func TestStrataSocketWritesOnEveryCellAcrossElections(t *testing.T) {
	w := harness.New(t)
	us, eu := w.Jurisdiction("us").Cell("us-1"), w.Jurisdiction("eu").Cell("eu-1")
	repo := w.Repo()
	us.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	eu.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	w.Settle()

	elected := time.Now().UTC()
	us.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	eu.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	w.Settle()

	socket := eu.API.OpensStrataSocket(repo)
	eu.AssertSocketWriteAcked(socket.Writes())

	moved := elected.Add(time.Minute)
	us.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, eu, moved))
	eu.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, eu, moved))
	w.Settle()

	eu.AssertSocketWriteAcked(socket.Writes())
}

// TestStrataRetentionInOneCellLeavesAnotherCellReading: us's writers drop
// generations from the strata repository both cells share. eu's projection
// stopped at one of them, and its next read still answers, with everything
// written since.
func TestStrataRetentionInOneCellLeavesAnotherCellReading(t *testing.T) {
	w := harness.New(t)
	us, eu := w.Jurisdiction("us").Cell("us-1"), w.Jurisdiction("eu").Cell("eu-1")
	repo := w.Repo()
	us.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	eu.Receives(events.RepoCreated(repo))
	w.Settle()
	elected := time.Now().UTC()
	us.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	eu.Receives(events.ProcessingPrimaryChanged(repo, us, elected))
	w.Settle()

	// Each session's start compacts what the last one wrote; 70 plans cross a
	// generation boundary.
	const perSession = 70
	sessions := 0
	session := func() {
		s := us.API.OpensStrataSocket(repo)
		us.AssertSocketWriteAcked(s.WritesPlans(perSession))
		s.Closes()
		sessions++
	}
	session()
	session()
	eu.SharesStrataRepoWith(us)
	us.API.OpensStrataSocket(repo).Closes()
	if got := eu.API.ReadsStrataPlans(repo); got != sessions*perSession {
		t.Fatalf("eu read %d plans, want %d", got, sessions*perSession)
	}
	_, stoppedAt := us.StrataGenerations()
	if stoppedAt == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no generation was published before eu read; the scenario needs one to drop")
	}

	for range 3 {
		session()
	}
	us.API.OpensStrataSocket(repo).Closes()
	us.AssertStrataGenerationDropped(stoppedAt)

	if got := eu.API.ReadsStrataPlans(repo); got != sessions*perSession {
		t.Errorf("after us dropped generation %d, eu read %d plans, want %d", stoppedAt, got, sessions*perSession)
	}
}

content.content:
[`docs/contributor-filed-records.md`](contributor-filed-records.md) argues that
`refs/meta/records/*` should be **excluded** from entiredb's server-side RSL,
because RSL reference entries are the push-activity signal (`ScanPushActivity`,
bounded by `repostat.ScanCap`), so recording metadata writes there would count
every comment as a push and shove real code pushes out of a capped window.

That argument is about a *statistic*, and it is correct. But policing these refs
requires the opposite: without RSL entries there is nothing for a verifier to
check, and a selectively-recorded ref is worse than an unrecorded one — a
verifier seeing A→C with no entry for B cannot tell it from tampering.

The two are reconcilable, and only one of the three ways is any good:

- **Filter the activity scan by ref name**, not the RSL by ref name. The signal
  wants code pushes; it should say so. One predicate in entiredb's
  `rslstore/activity.go`, and the cap then bounds the thing it was meant to
  bound.
- A **second RSL** for records refs. Coherent, and doubles the thing a verifier
  has to know about.
- Leave the exclusion and accept that per-type rules are unenforceable. Which is
  the current position, and is fine right up until someone wants a read-only
  type.

Recommendation: the first. It is a smaller change than this proposal's own
prerequisites, and it makes the exclusion unnecessary rather than conditional.

## What to do first

**The ref-level rule is worth having on its own.** `git:refs/meta/records/*`
buys "who may write this store at all" for items 2 and 3 only — no commit
signing, no per-type nuance, nothing to decide about `children`,
because a `git:` rule never looks inside a commit. It is also the increment that makes the RSL
question concrete, and it is useful without any of what follows.

Per-type rules need all four items, and item 4 before any code: whether the
engine-maintained indices are inside or outside a type's write boundary.

## Rejected

**A ref per type**, so ordinary ref permissions suffice and no file rules or
commit signing are needed. It fails on the same rock as the quarantine design in
`contributor-filed-records.md`: `WriteBatch.Resolve` reads the store it writes —
`resolveExisting`, `nextRank` over siblings, `verifyReferences` — so a child on
one ref whose parent is on another cannot resolve its rank or its references. It
also multiplies the contention surface this store is built around, and costs the
property that a plain `git fetch` gives you everything.

**Authorization in the schema.** Already rejected, for the reason
`contributor-filed-records.md` gives: it puts a server concept into a language
whose premise is that there is no server. Nothing here changes that. The
difference is only that gittuf can now express more of it than that doc credited
— which strengthens the case for keeping it out of the schema, not weakens it.

**Enforcement in `WriteBatch`.** An engine-side check refuses the writes it is
asked to make, and anyone able to bypass it has push access, which is to say has
the ability to write the ref directly. It would be a usability feature wearing a
security feature's clothes. If the refusal is wanted for its error message, it
belongs next to the schema as advice — the `knownValues` precedent
(`docs/adrs/20260726-known-values-are-advertised-not-enforced.md`) — and not as
a claim about who can do what.
